q: 在线拍卖系统（类 eBay）的三条核心功能需求是？
q_en: What are the three core functional requirements for an eBay-style online auction system?
options: 发布拍卖（起拍价+结束时间）、出价（只接受更高出价）、查看当前最高价
支持用户按关键词搜索商品、按类目筛选结果、并按价格从低到高排序展示
允许发布拍卖、自动代扣支付完成订单结算、并对接第三方物流公司跟踪配送
开放出价、可查看完整历史成交记录、并允许买家给卖家留言打分评价
why: 核心三条：发布带起拍价和结束时间的拍卖、出价（只有高于当前最高价才接受）、查看拍卖和当前最高价。搜索/过滤/排序/历史都划到范围外。
why_en: The three core requirements are posting an auction, bidding above the current highest bid, and viewing the current highest bid.
options_en: Post an auction with a starting price and end date, accept only higher bids, and view the current highest bid.
Let users search for items by keyword, filter results by category, and sort them from low to high price.
Let users post auctions, automatically settle payment for the order, and track shipment with a third-party carrier.
Open bidding, show the full historical sale record, and let buyers leave a rating and comment for sellers.
optionExplanations: 这三件事撑起最小拍卖闭环——发布、出价、看价，缺一个都没法成交。
这组是商品发现体验，属于范围外的浏览功能，不是拍卖本身要做的事。
这组混入了结算和物流，那是成交之后的履约环节，本题只到出价为止。
这组漏了发布拍卖，换成历史记录和信誉评分，都是范围外的附加功能。
optionExplanations_en: These three actions form the minimum auction loop — posting, bidding, and viewing price — miss one and there's no deal.
This set is item-discovery browsing, explicitly out of scope, not the auction's own loop.
This mixes in payment settlement and shipping, which belong to post-sale fulfillment, past where this problem stops.
This drops auction creation and swaps in history and ratings, both out-of-scope extras.
scenario: 45 分钟面试设计 eBay 式在线拍卖，时间只够覆盖最小成交闭环，浏览发现类功能一律砍掉。
scenario_en: You have 45 minutes to design an eBay-style auction, so you only have room for the minimum end-to-end selling loop and have to cut all the browsing and discovery features.

q: 在线拍卖系统设计里，以下哪些功能被划为「范围外」（below the line）？（多选）
q_en: In this online auction design, which features are below the line and out of scope?
options: 按类别过滤商品
对某个拍卖出价
查看某商品的拍卖历史
按价格排序商品
why: 搜索、过滤、排序、历史查看都是范围外；出价是三大核心功能之一，也是这道题最值得深挖的部分。
why_en: Search, filtering, sorting, and auction history are out of scope, while bidding is a core requirement.
options_en: Filter items by category.
Place a bid on an auction.
View an item's auction history.
Sort items by price.
optionExplanations: 范围外——商品发现体验，跟出价流程无关，本题不展开。
范围内——出价是三条核心功能之一，不属于要排除的功能。
范围外——完整历史查询留到后续版本，不是这轮要做的事。
范围外——排序同属商品浏览体验，跟本题的竞价核心无关。
optionExplanations_en: Out of scope — item-discovery UX unrelated to the bidding flow this problem covers.
In scope — bidding is one of the three core requirements, not something to exclude.
Out of scope — full history browsing is deferred, not part of this pass.
Out of scope — sorting is browsing UX, unrelated to the core bidding decision.
scenario: 在线拍卖面试要求把设计火力全押在竞价竞态上，凡是不影响成交正确性的功能都推到线下。
scenario_en: The interviewer wants you to spend the whole session on bidding race conditions, so anything that doesn't affect whether a sale is correct gets pushed below the line.

q: 在线拍卖平台（类 eBay）的核心非功能需求包括哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which non-functional requirements matter most for an eBay-style online auction platform?
options: 竞价要强一致，所有人看到同一个最高价
容错且持久，一条出价都不能丢
实时展示当前最高价
所有读写都必须在 1ms 内完成
why: 四条核心 NFR：竞价强一致、容错持久（不丢 bid）、实时最高价、支撑 1000 万并发拍卖。没有「1ms 内完成」这种要求。
why_en: The core requirements are strong consistency for bids, fault tolerance so no bid is dropped, and real-time display of the highest bid — not millisecond-level latency.
options_en: Bidding must be strongly consistent so everyone sees the same highest bid.
The system must be fault-tolerant and durable; no bid can be dropped.
The current highest bid must be displayed in real time.
Every read and write must complete within 1 millisecond.
optionExplanations: 强一致防的是双人都以为自己出价最高的分裂结果。
容错持久防的是一条出价被悄悄丢掉、赢家凭空消失。
实时展示防的是用户拿着过期价格出价、被莫名拒绝。
误读——题目没给毫秒级延迟指标，这条约束是编出来的。
optionExplanations_en: Strong consistency prevents two bidders both believing they're currently winning.
Fault tolerance and durability prevent a bid from silently vanishing and costing someone the win.
Real-time display prevents users bidding against a price that's already stale.
Misread — the prompt sets no millisecond-level latency target; this constraint is invented.
scenario: eBay 式拍卖要撑住 1000 万并发拍卖，出价关系到钱、一条都不能丢，收官前几秒流量会飙升。
scenario_en: The eBay-style auction has to hold ten million concurrent auctions, bids are money so we can't drop a single one, and traffic spikes in the last few seconds before an auction closes.

q: 这个规模数字最先决定了后续设计的哪个环节？
q_en: Which later design step is driven first by this scale target?
options: 决定 API 网关要不要开启身份鉴权和限流策略
决定后续吞吐、存储量级的估算基准，并牵出分片决策
决定前端页面该用哪种 UI 组件库渲染
决定要不要给某张数据库表加一个索引
why: 规模锚点是 1000 万并发拍卖，后面所有吞吐、存储、分片的估算都从这个数字推出来——不是选前端框架或加索引这类局部决策。
why_en: The ten-million concurrent-auction target anchors all later throughput, storage, and sharding math, not narrow choices like frontend frameworks.
scenario: 面试官给出的规模目标是：系统要支撑 1000 万个并发拍卖，且要扛住热门拍卖收官前的瞬时流量高峰。
scenario_en: The interviewer gives a scale target: support 10 million concurrent auctions and handle traffic spikes near the end of hot auctions.
options_en: It decides whether the API gateway turns on authentication and rate limiting.
It anchors later throughput and storage estimates, and drives sharding decisions.
It decides which UI component library renders the frontend page.
It decides whether to add an index to some database table.
optionExplanations: 鉴权限流是接口安全策略，不看并发拍卖数这个规模锚点。
这才是规模数字真正的用途——后续容量和分片怎么估都由它打底。
前端组件库选型是团队偏好问题，跟并发拍卖数无关。
加不加索引看查询模式，不是靠一个顶层并发数字决定。
optionExplanations_en: Gateway auth and rate limiting are API-security policy, unrelated to the concurrent-auction target.
This is the number's real job — it seeds the later capacity and partitioning math down the line.
Choosing a frontend component library is a team preference, not driven by concurrency scale.
Adding an index depends on query patterns, not on one top-level concurrency number.

q: 系统设计面试进入非功能需求环节之前，你应该先向面试官确认什么？
q_en: Before discussing non-functional requirements, what should you clarify with the interviewer?
options: 先画完整架构图
先问面试官预期的系统规模
先写 API 定义
先估算存储成本
why: 先问清预期规模：规模决定后面一系列关键架构决策（要不要分片、要不要消息队列等），越早知道越好。
why_en: Ask about expected scale early because it drives key architectural decisions like sharding and message queues throughout the design.
options_en: Draw out the complete architecture diagram first.
Ask the interviewer about the expected system scale.
Write out the API definitions first.
Estimate storage costs first.
optionExplanations: 画架构图要等规模明确后再做，否则服务边界大概率要返工。
问清规模能定下后面要不要分片、上队列、加缓存等一连串决策。
API 设计适合等实体和主流程理清后再写，不能替代规模澄清。
算存储成本得先有对象数量和增长率，这些数字没问规模就没有。
optionExplanations_en: Drawing the architecture should wait for scale, or service boundaries likely get redone.
Clarifying scale up front decides a whole chain of later calls — sharding, queues, caching.
API design fits once entities and the core flow are clear; it can't substitute for asking scale.
Storage cost math needs object counts and growth rates — numbers you don't have without asking scale first.
scenario: 在线拍卖面试刚敲定功能需求，要不要分片、要不要上消息队列全悬着，只差一个未知量。
scenario_en: You've just locked down functional requirements for the auction system, and whether you shard or bring in a message queue is still open — it all hinges on one unknown.

q: 补全在线拍卖系统的四个核心实体：
q_en: Fill in the four core entities of the online auction system.
text: 四个核心实体：{{Auction}}（拍卖：起拍价、结束时间）、{{Item}}（商品：名称、描述、图片）、{{Bid}}（出价：金额、出价人、所属拍卖）、{{User}}（发起拍卖或出价的用户）。
why: 先把实体列出来、细节从简，能帮后面 API 设计搭好骨架。Auction 与 Item 分开建模，Bid 通过 auctionId 关联拍卖。
why_en: The four core entities are Auction, Item, Bid, and User, kept light up front to structure the API design that follows.

termDefinitions.meaning: 拍卖实体，含起拍价、结束时间、所拍商品。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An Auction holds the starting price, end date, and the item being sold.

termDefinitions.meaning: 商品实体，含名称、描述、图片。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An Item holds the name, description, and images of a product.

termDefinitions.meaning: 出价实体，含金额、出价人、所属拍卖。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Bid holds the amount, the bidder, and which auction it belongs to.

termDefinitions.meaning: 发起拍卖或出价的用户实体。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A User is the account that starts an auction or places a bid.

scenario: 建模时纠结：把 Item 的字段直接内嵌进 Auction，还是拆成独立实体？卖家常会把流拍的商品重新上架。
scenario_en: During modeling, you are choosing between embedding Item fields inside Auction or making Item a separate entity; sellers often relist unsold items.
q: 把 Item 规范化成独立实体的主要好处是？
q_en: What is the main benefit of normalizing Item into a separate entity?
options: 查询拍卖详情时不用做表 join，读取路径更简单更快
商品可跨多个拍卖复用、可独立更新、更容易加类目/搜索等商品级功能
把商品字段拆开能显著节省数据库总存储空间
把 Item 独立出来能避免出价时的并发竞态条件
why: 拆开的三个好处：商品可在多个拍卖间复用（重新上架）、商品详情可独立于拍卖更新、便于扩展类目/搜索等商品级功能。内嵌反而免了 join。
why_en: Normalizing Item into its own entity lets items be reused across auctions, updated independently, and extended with item-level features.
whenOtherWins: 内嵌进 Auction 也可接受——更简单、读时无需 join；面试里两种都行，关键是把理由讲清楚。
options_en: Queries won't need a table join, so reads are simpler and faster.
Items can be reused across auctions, updated independently, and extended with item-level features like categories or search.
Splitting item fields out saves significant database storage.
Separating Item avoids race conditions when bids are placed.
tradeoff: 跨拍卖复用与独立演进 vs 内嵌免 join 的读取简单性

termDefinitions.meaning: 把字段拆到独立实体/表，减少重复、便于独立更新。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Normalizing means splitting fields into a separate entity or table so they can be reused and updated independently.

termDefinitions.meaning: 关系型数据库里把多张表按关联字段合并查询的操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A join combines rows from multiple tables based on a related key during a query.

optionExplanations: 读路径极热、商品从不复用时，内嵌字段更值——省一次 join，但复用和独立演进就没了。
商品会重新上架、需要独立更新或扩展类目搜索时，拆成独立实体最合适。
只有字段大量重复、存储成本主导时才值得为此拆分；这里差距不大，不是主因。
出价竞态发生在并发写最高价的路径上，跟 Item 是否独立建模无关。
optionExplanations_en: Embedding fields wins when reads are extremely hot and items are never reused — you save a join but lose reuse and independent updates.
A separate Item entity fits when products get relisted, updated on their own, or extended with category and search features.
Splitting only pays off when duplicated fields dominate storage cost; here the gap is too small to be the real driver.
Bid races happen on the concurrent highest-price write path, unrelated to whether Item is its own entity.

q: 创建拍卖的 API 请求体里应包含哪些字段？
q_en: Which fields should the create-auction API request body include?
options: item、startDate、endDate、startingPrice
auctionId、maxBid、userId
item、category、sortOrder
startingPrice、buyNowPrice、shippingFee
why: POST /auctions 带上商品信息、起止时间和起拍价，返回创建好的 Auction & Item。这直接对应功能需求一。
why_en: Creating an auction is a POST to /auctions with the item, start and end dates, and starting price.
codeSample:
POST /auctions -> Auction & Item
{
    item: Item,
    startDate: Date,
    endDate: Date,
    startingPrice: number
}
options_en: item, startDate, endDate, startingPrice
auctionId, maxBid, userId
item, category, sortOrder
startingPrice, buyNowPrice, shippingFee
optionExplanations: 这组就是创建拍卖要传的字段——商品、起止时间、起拍价，缺一不可。
这组是拍卖建好之后才有的东西，创建请求体里不会带 auctionId。
这组是搜索列表页用的过滤排序参数，创建拍卖不需要传排序方式。
buyNowPrice 和 shippingFee 这题没定义一口价和运费功能，别混进来。
optionExplanations_en: These are exactly the create-auction fields — item, time window, starting price, nothing skippable.
These only exist after the auction is created; the create request can't carry an auctionId yet.
These are search-page filter and sort params; creating an auction doesn't need a sort order.
buyNowPrice and shippingFee assume features this problem never defines — don't smuggle them in.
scenario: 在线拍卖的发布接口只有一次请求机会：定价和倒计时都必须在这个请求里一次定死。
scenario_en: The auction creation endpoint gets exactly one shot — the price floor and the countdown both have to be fixed in that single request.

q: 出价（placing a bid）的 API 应该怎么设计？
q_en: How should the API for placing a bid be modeled?
options: PUT /auctions/:auctionId 更新 maxBid 字段，不生成新的出价记录
POST /bids，请求体里带 auctionId 表示归属哪场拍卖
GET /auctions/:auctionId/bid?amount=100，把出价塞进查询参数
POST /auctions/:auctionId/bids，请求体带 Bid 详情，返回创建的 Bid
why: 出价是在某个拍卖下创建一条 Bid 资源，所以用嵌套路径 POST /auctions/:auctionId/bids，返回创建的 Bid（含接受/拒绝状态）。
why_en: Placing a bid is a POST to /auctions/:auctionId/bids with the bid details, returning the created bid.
options_en: PUT /auctions/:auctionId and update the maxBid field, creating no new bid record.
POST /bids with auctionId in the request body to say which auction it belongs to.
GET /auctions/:auctionId/bid?amount=100, packing the bid into a query parameter.
POST /auctions/:auctionId/bids with the bid details, returning the created bid.

termDefinitions.term: 嵌套资源路径 (nested resource path)
termDefinitions.meaning: URL 里把从属资源放在父资源路径下，如 /auctions/:id/bids 表示 bid 属于某个 auction。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A nested resource path places a child resource under its parent in the URL, like /auctions/:id/bids for a bid that belongs to an auction.

optionExplanations: 覆盖字段等于只认最新价，出价历史和拒绝记录全部丢失。
扁平路径能工作，但拍卖归属只能靠请求体里的字段间接表达。
GET 该用来读数据，出价是写操作，不能拿查询参数悄悄改状态。
嵌套在拍卖下创建 Bid，路径和方法都直接说清了这是一次出价写入。
optionExplanations_en: Overwriting a field means only the latest price survives — bid history and rejections vanish.
A flat path can work, but the auction relationship only lives inside the request body, not the URL.
GET is for reads; bidding is a write and shouldn't smuggle state changes into query params.
Nesting Bid creation under the auction makes both the path and verb say exactly what's happening.
scenario: 在线拍卖里每次出价都要留下可审计记录，而且一条出价天然只从属于某一场拍卖。
scenario_en: Every bid in the auction system has to leave an auditable record, and a bid only ever belongs to one specific auction.

q: 查看拍卖页时，GET /auctions/:auctionId 返回什么？
q_en: When rendering an auction page, what should GET /auctions/:auctionId return?
options: 只有 Auction
Auction 和完整的 Bid 列表
Auction 与 Item 详情
只有当前最高价数字
why: 查看拍卖需要商品信息 + 拍卖信息（含当前最高价）用于页面展示，所以返回 Auction & Item；完整出价历史被划在范围外。
why_en: Viewing an auction is a GET that returns the auction and item details needed to render the page.
options_en: Only the Auction.
The Auction and the full list of Bids.
The Auction and Item details.
Only the current highest-bid number.
optionExplanations: 只查内部状态时够用，但页面渲染还缺商品名称、图片这些信息。
完整出价历史留给专门的历史页做，本题把它划到范围外。
页面要同时展示商品详情和拍卖状态，当前最高价本来就在 Auction 里。
价格小组件够用，但完整详情页还要名称、描述、图片这些商品信息。
optionExplanations_en: This fits an internal status check, but the page still needs item name and images to render.
A full bid list belongs on a dedicated history page, which this problem puts out of scope.
The page needs item details alongside auction state, and the highest bid already lives on Auction.
A price widget could use just the number, but the full page still needs name, description, images.
scenario: 拍卖详情页要一次渲染出商品和当前最高价，而完整出价历史被明确划到范围外。
scenario_en: The auction detail page has to render the item and the current highest bid in one shot, and the full bid history is explicitly out of scope.

q: 在高层设计里，API Gateway 承担哪些职责？
q_en: In the high-level design, what does the API Gateway own?
options: 只负责存储拍卖数据、执行出价合法性校验
鉴权、限流、以及最重要的——把请求路由到对应服务
维护每个用户的 SSE 长连接，向客户端广播新出价
计算并写入拍卖当前的最高出价
why: API Gateway 是客户端进后端的统一入口：做鉴权、限流，最重要的是把请求路由到 Auction Service 或 Bidding Service。
why_en: The API gateway handles authentication and rate limiting, and most importantly routes each request to the right service.
options_en: Only store auction data and validate bid legality.
Authentication, rate limiting, and most importantly, routing requests to the right service.
Maintain each user's SSE connection and broadcast new bids to clients.
Compute and write the auction's current highest bid.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端请求进入后端的统一入口，常做鉴权、限流、路由。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API gateway is the single entry point for client requests, typically handling auth, rate limiting, and routing.

termDefinitions.meaning: Server-Sent Events，服务器向客户端单向推送更新的长连接技术。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE, or Server-Sent Events, lets a server push updates to a client over a long-lived one-way connection.

optionExplanations: 存储和业务校验是后端服务的活，网关不该掌管拍卖状态。
网关在入口层做鉴权限流这些横切逻辑，再把请求送去对的服务。
长连接推送是专门的实时层要做的事，不是普通请求网关的职责。
算最高价是出价服务写路径里的业务逻辑，网关不参与。
optionExplanations_en: Storage and business validation belong to backend services; the gateway shouldn't own auction state.
The gateway handles cross-cutting entry logic like auth and rate limiting, then routes each request onward.
Long-lived push connections belong to a dedicated real-time layer, not a plain request gateway.
Computing the highest bid is write-path business logic that lives in the bidding service, not the gateway.
scenario: 在线拍卖后端已拆成 Auction Service 和 Bidding Service，客户端只想连一个地址。
scenario_en: The auction backend is already split into an Auction Service and a Bidding Service, but the client only wants one address to talk to.

q: 把「创建一个新拍卖」的数据流排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the create-auction data flow in the correct order.
steps: Auction Service 校验请求，写入拍卖和商品数据
客户端向 /auctions 发送 POST 请求
数据库把数据存入 auctions 和 items 表
API Gateway 把请求路由到 Auction Service
why: 创建拍卖就是基本 CRUD：客户端 POST → 网关路由 → Auction Service 校验并写入 → 数据库落表。此时 Auction Service 只是数据库的薄封装。
why_en: Creating an auction flows from the client's POST through the gateway to the auction service, which validates and writes the data to the database.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    C[Client] -->|POST /auctions| G[API Gateway]
    G --> A[Auction Service]
    A -->|校验+写入| D[(Database)]

scenario: 拍卖商品带图片，但面试时间有限，图片存储不是这道题的重点。
scenario_en: Auction items include images, but interview time is limited and image storage is not the hard part of this problem.
q: 对商品图片的正确处理方式是？
q_en: How should product images be handled in this auction design?
options: 把图片原始二进制数据直接写进 items 表字段，不做任何拆分，字段会越来越大
现场花 10 分钟设计完整的图片上传、压缩、分发管线，挤占核心讨论时间
图片放 blob 存储、items 表存 URL 引用，并跟面试官说明这不是重点
完全不提图片存储方案，假装这不是问题的一部分，容易被面试官追问
why: 标准做法：图片进 blob 存储、表里存 URL 引用。这不是本题最有意思的部分，主动跟面试官对齐「不深入」以节省时间。
why_en: Store images in blob storage referenced by URL, and tell the interviewer this is intentionally not the focus.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试题本身就是图片/媒体系统（如 Instagram），上传管线、CDN 分发才值得展开。
options_en: Write the raw image bytes directly into a field on the items table, which keeps growing.
Spend ten interview minutes designing a full image upload pipeline, eating into core discussion time.
Store images in blob storage, keep only a URL in the items table, and tell the interviewer this isn't the focus.
Never mention image storage at all, as if the problem didn't exist, and invite a follow-up question.
tradeoff: 把时间花在拍卖核心难点 vs 深入图片上传管线

termDefinitions.meaning: 用于存放图片、视频等大二进制文件的存储服务，如 S3。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Blob storage is an object store for large binary files like images and video, such as S3.

optionExplanations: 小图标或后台工具或许能这样干；商品图片会拖慢整张表和备份。
这套投入值得留给媒体类考题；这里会占用竞价一致性的讨论时间。
对象存储放图、表里留 URL，覆盖了需求又没抢走核心讨论的时间。
完全不提图片存储像是漏了需求，一句话交代边界比沉默更稳。
optionExplanations_en: This might fit a tiny icon or admin tool; product photos would bloat the table and every backup.
That depth belongs to a media-focused interview; here it eats into time meant for bid consistency.
Object storage for the bytes plus a URL column covers the need without stealing time from the real discussion.
Saying nothing about images reads like a missed requirement; one boundary sentence is safer than silence.

scenario: 出价流量预计是创建拍卖流量的约 100 倍，且出价有复杂的校验、竞态、实时更新逻辑。
scenario_en: Bid traffic is expected to be about 100x auction-creation traffic, and bidding has validation, race-condition, and real-time update logic.
q: 为什么要把 Bidding Service 从 Auction Service 里拆出来？
q_en: Why split Bidding Service out from Auction Service?
options: 拆开能独立扩容、隔离复杂业务逻辑、并分别按写密集/读密集优化
微服务架构在任何规模下都天然优于单体应用
关系型数据库设计规范要求每张表对应一个独立服务
拆分单纯是为了让 API Gateway 的路由规则更简单
why: 三个理由：出价量约是创建量的 100 倍需要独立扩容；出价的校验/竞态/实时更新逻辑复杂，值得隔离；Bidding 可按高吞吐写优化、Auction 按读密集优化。
why_en: A separate bidding service allows independent scaling, isolates complex bidding logic, and lets each service be optimized for its own workload.
whenOtherWins: 如果规模很小、团队很小，单一服务更简单——服务拆分本身有运维成本，没有量级差异时不必拆。
options_en: Splitting it out enables independent scaling, isolates complex logic, and lets each service optimize for its own read/write pattern.
Microservices are always better than a monolith at any scale.
Relational database design requires one service per table.
The split exists purely to simplify the API gateway's routing rules.
tradeoff: 独立扩容+逻辑隔离 vs 单一服务的运维简单性
optionExplanations: 写量和业务复杂度明显分叉时，拆开才能各自扩容、各自调优。
团队和规模都很小时，单体往往更省心；这句话把结论说绝对了。
表结构不决定服务边界，边界该看流量、逻辑复杂度和团队归属。
网关确实能路由到多个服务，但路由简单从来不是拆分的主要理由。
optionExplanations_en: When write volume and logic complexity clearly diverge, splitting lets each side scale and tune on its own.
For a small team at small scale, a monolith is often simpler — this claim overstates it as an absolute.
Table structure doesn't define service boundaries; traffic, logic complexity, and which team runs it do.
The gateway can route to multiple services fine, but simpler routing was never the main reason to split.

q: 出价（bids）流量和拍卖创建流量的量级关系大约是？
q_en: Roughly how does bid traffic compare with auction-creation traffic?
options: 差不多 1:1
出价约是创建的 10 倍
出价约是创建的 100 倍
创建比出价多
why: 每个拍卖生命周期约 100 次出价，所以出价流量 ≈ 100 倍于拍卖创建流量——这是拆出独立 Bidding Service 的量化依据。
why_en: Bid traffic runs roughly a hundred times auction-creation traffic, which justifies scaling the bidding service independently.
scenario: 已知每个拍卖平均收到约 100 次出价；面试官想确认你能否把这个假设换算成流量估算。
scenario_en: Assume each auction receives about 100 bids on average; the interviewer wants you to turn that assumption into a traffic estimate.
options_en: Roughly 1:1.
Bids are about ten times auction creation.
Bids are about a hundred times auction creation.
Creation traffic is higher than bidding.
optionExplanations: 这个比例太低估了单场拍卖里出价的活跃程度。
方向对但量级低估了——真实场景通常远不止十倍。
每场拍卖平均约 100 次出价，这个比例是拆分服务的量化依据。
这个说法反了——出价明显比创建拍卖频繁得多。
optionExplanations_en: This ratio badly underestimates how active bidding gets within one auction.
Right direction, wrong magnitude — the real gap runs well past ten times.
About 100 bids per auction on average, and that ratio is the number behind splitting the service.
This has it backwards — bidding happens far more often than creating auctions.

q: Bidding Service 负责哪些事情？（多选）
q_en: Which responsibilities belong to the Bidding Service?
options: 校验进来的出价（是否高于当前最高价）
把拍卖的最高价更新为新出价
把出价历史写入数据库
托管商品图片
why: Bidding Service 四件事：校验出价、更新拍卖最高价、存出价历史、通知相关方。图片属于 blob 存储，不归它管。
why_en: The bidding service validates bids, updates the auction's highest bid, and stores bid history — not image hosting.
options_en: Validate the incoming bid (check it beats the current highest).
Update the auction's highest bid to the new bid.
Write bid history to the database.
Host item images.
optionExplanations: 挡住无效出价——价格没超过当前最高价的请求直接被拒。
保证页面看到的最高价始终是最新写入的那个数字。
留住审计证据——不管接受还是拒绝，每条出价都要能查得到。
不归它管——图片托管属于 blob 存储，混进出价服务会越权。
optionExplanations_en: Blocks invalid bids — anything not above the current highest gets rejected on the spot.
Keeps the displayed highest bid always in sync with the latest accepted write.
Preserves audit evidence — every bid, accepted or rejected, stays traceable.
Not its job — image hosting belongs to blob storage, not the bidding service.
scenario: 在线拍卖把出价拆成独立服务，因为出价流量约是创建拍卖的 100 倍且带竞态校验。
scenario_en: Bidding got its own service because bid traffic is roughly a hundred times the auction-creation traffic and carries all the race-condition validation.

q: 简单版出价流程中，Bidding Service 收到出价后做什么？
q_en: In the simple bidding flow, what does Bidding Service do after receiving a bid?
options: 直接覆盖拍卖上的最高价字段，不保留任何出价记录到数据库，历史全部丢失
查当前最高价，按 accepted/rejected 状态写入 bids 表
先把出价塞进内存队列缓冲，攒够一批之后再统一批量处理，有延迟风险
只有当出价通过校验被接受时，才把这条记录写入数据库，拒绝的没留痕
why: 关键点：无论接受还是拒绝，出价都要落到 bids 表（带状态），并通过 auctionId 关联拍卖，然后把结果告诉用户。
why_en: The bidding service reads the current highest bid, stores the new bid as accepted or rejected, and returns that status to the client.
options_en: Overwrite the highest-bid field directly and keep no bid record in the database at all, losing all history.
Read the current highest bid, then write it to the bids table as accepted or rejected.
Push the bid into an in-memory queue and process it later in a batch, risking delay.
Only write to the database when the bid passes validation and is accepted, leaving rejections untraced.
optionExplanations: 这是玩具系统的做法，出价没有留痕，真实拍卖需要能审计。
先比对当前最高价，再把结果按 accepted/rejected 落进 bids 表。
攒批处理适合能容忍延迟的写入，出价不能因为进程崩了就丢。
只存被接受的记录，被拒绝的出价没有证据，纠纷说不清楚。
optionExplanations_en: That's a toy-system move — nothing gets recorded, and real auctions need an audit trail.
Compare against the current highest first, then persist the result as accepted or rejected in bids.
Batching fits writes that can tolerate delay; a bid can't just disappear if the process crashes.
Storing only accepted bids leaves rejected ones with no evidence, so disputes go unresolved.
scenario: 在线拍卖要求事后可仲裁：即使一次出价被拒，也得能回溯它当时为什么被拒。
scenario_en: The auction system has to support dispute resolution after the fact — even a rejected bid has to be traceable to why it was rejected.

q: 只在 Auction 上存一个 maxBidPrice 字段、每次覆盖更新，而不维护 bids 表，会带来什么后果？
q_en: What happens if Auction only stores maxBidPrice and overwrites it instead of keeping a bids table?
options: 写入路径多了一次字段更新，写入性能会略微下降，几乎可以忽略不计
销毁历史数据——没法审计竞价、查纠纷，用户投诉「出价没被记录」时无法自证
覆盖后最高价字段本身会被算错，出现负数或空值，这属于代码逻辑缺陷
所有历史出价都保留只会让数据库存储占用暴涨，需要额外归档策略
why: 覆盖式更新违反了数据完整性的核心原则：不要销毁历史数据。没有完整审计记录，就没法处理纠纷或分析行为模式。
why_en: Overwriting a single max-bid field destroys the audit trail, so disputes can't be investigated and a user's bid can't be proven handled correctly.
options_en: The write path gains one extra field update, so write performance drops slightly — barely worth worrying about.
It destroys historical data — you can't audit bidding or investigate disputes, and can't disprove a user who claims their bid was never recorded.
Overwriting makes the highest-bid field itself compute incorrectly, producing nulls or negative values, which is a code defect.
Keeping every historical bid would make database storage explode, needing an extra archiving strategy.
optionExplanations: 极端写吞吐瓶颈时才该先担心这个；这里的真风险不是性能。
覆盖式更新把出价轨迹全抹了，纠纷和审计都没证据可查。
字段算错通常是代码逻辑 bug，跟只存一个覆盖字段没关系。
保留历史确实吃存储，但拍卖出价通常值得为可追责多花这点空间。
optionExplanations_en: That's only the real concern under an extreme write bottleneck; the actual risk here isn't performance.
Overwriting wipes the whole bid trail, leaving no evidence for disputes or audits.
Miscalculated fields are usually a code bug, unrelated to storing just one overwritten field.
History does cost storage, but auction bids are usually worth that space for accountability.
scenario: 在线拍卖平台要处理买卖纠纷、还要分析刷价行为，出价数据必须能事后追溯。
scenario_en: The auction platform has to settle buyer-seller disputes and analyze shill-bidding patterns, so bid data has to be reconstructable after the fact.

q: 用户查看拍卖页有两个动机，它们对系统的要求有何不同？
q_en: How do the two reasons for viewing an auction page create different system requirements?
options: 了解商品是只读操作；而准备出价需要实时一致的当前最高价
了解商品和准备出价都只需要最终一致就够，出价校验容易出错
了解商品和准备出价都必须强一致才行，等于把成本都拉满了
了解商品需要实时一致，出价反而不需要，这个判断正好反了
why: 看商品详情是普通只读；但要出价就必须知道「要打败的那个最高价」，这需要实时一致——两个相似的动作、不同的一致性要求。
why_en: Learning about the item is read-only, but preparing to bid needs real-time knowledge of the current highest bid.
options_en: Learning about the item is a read-only action, while preparing to bid needs a real-time-consistent view of the current highest bid.
Both learning about the item and preparing to bid only need eventual consistency, making bid validation error-prone.
Both learning about the item and preparing to bid require strong consistency, maxing out the cost for no reason.
Learning about the item needs real-time consistency, but bidding doesn't — which has it exactly backwards.
optionExplanations: 浏览商品是普通只读；出价前必须知道要打败的那个最新价。
浏览确实能容忍旧数据，但出价用最终一致会导致误判被拒。
把商品详情也做成强一致纯属浪费，压力其实只来自出价前那一刻。
这个说法把两者反了——实时压力恰恰来自出价，不是浏览商品。
optionExplanations_en: Browsing the item is a plain read; bidding needs the latest price you're trying to beat.
Browsing can tolerate staleness, but eventual consistency on bidding causes bad rejections.
Making item details strongly consistent too is wasted cost; the pressure only comes from the bid moment.
This flips it — the freshness pressure comes from bidding, not from browsing the item.
scenario: 拍卖详情页同时服务只看热闹的人和马上要出价的人，两者对价格新鲜度要求不同。
scenario_en: The auction detail page serves both people just browsing and people about to bid, and those two have very different tolerance for a stale price.

q: 如果拍卖页从不刷新最高价，会发生什么？
q_en: What happens if the auction page never refreshes the current highest bid?
options: 数据库读请求负载会明显升高，这其实是主动轮询才会有的代价
用户按过时价格出价，被拒后困惑沮丧，热门拍卖尤其明显
同一个用户的出价会被系统重复提交两次，这要靠幂等键解决
拍卖到了结束时间也无法正常关闭，这跟页面刷不刷新无关
why: 价格陈旧 → 用户按旧价出价 → 系统拒绝 → 用户困惑。初版解法是每隔几秒轮询一次最新最高价，不完美但能显著减少这种情况。
why_en: Without refreshing, users bid against a stale price and get confusing rejections, so the fix is polling the latest max bid every few seconds.
options_en: Database read load rises noticeably, which is really just the cost of active polling.
Users bid against a stale price and get confused and frustrated when rejected — especially bad on hot auctions.
The same user's bid gets submitted twice by the system, a job for an idempotency key.
The auction can never close even after its end time passes, unrelated to page refreshing.
optionExplanations: 这是轮询带来的代价；完全不刷新反而是发的请求变少了。
用户看着旧价出手，一被拒就以为系统出了故障，热门拍卖更明显。
重复提交要靠幂等键防，跟要不要刷新最高价是两码事。
拍卖能不能关，看的是结束时间和后台任务，不看页面刷不刷新。
optionExplanations_en: That's the cost of polling; never refreshing actually sends fewer requests, not more.
Users bid against a price that's gone stale, and the rejection feels like a bug — worse on hot auctions.
Duplicate submits need an idempotency key; refreshing the price has nothing to do with that.
Whether an auction closes depends on end time and backend jobs, not on page refreshes.
scenario: 热门拍卖收官前几秒价格连跳，而详情页只在打开那一刻取过一次最高价。
scenario_en: In the last few seconds of a hot auction the price jumps repeatedly, but the detail page only fetched the highest bid once, when it opened.

q: 多个用户同时对同一拍卖出价、只能有一个赢——这对应哪个系统设计模式？
q_en: When multiple users bid on the same auction and only one can win, which design pattern is this?
options: 实时更新（Real-time Updates）模式——服务器主动推送最新状态给客户端
扇出（Fan-out）模式——一条写入需要分发给大量下游读者
处理竞争（Dealing with Contention）模式——多方争抢同一资源时的协调
CQRS 模式——把读路径和写路径拆成两套独立模型
why: 在线拍卖是「处理竞争」模式的经典案例：多方争夺同一资源产生竞态，需要乐观并发控制、行锁或缓存策略来协调。
why_en: Simultaneous bids on the same auction are a textbook dealing-with-contention pattern, coordinated with tools like optimistic concurrency control or row locking.
options_en: Real-time Updates pattern — the server proactively pushes the latest state to clients.
Fan-out pattern — one write must be distributed to a large number of downstream readers.
Dealing with Contention pattern — coordinating multiple parties competing for the same resource.
CQRS pattern — splitting the read path and write path into two separate models.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一条写入需要分发/通知给大量下游读者或订阅者。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out means one write must be distributed or delivered to a large number of downstream readers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 命令查询职责分离，把系统的读路径和写路径拆成两套独立模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CQRS, or Command Query Responsibility Segregation, splits a system's read model from its write model.

optionExplanations: 通知旁观者最新状态才是它的主场，这里的问题是谁能赢。
一条写要分发给大量订阅者才是它的主场，出价不是广播问题。
多个写者同时抢一个最高价名额，这正是处理竞争模式要解决的事。
CQRS 帮读写模型分别扩展，但它不负责判定谁的出价赢了。
optionExplanations_en: Its home turf is notifying bystanders of new state; the problem here is deciding who wins.
Its home turf is delivering one write to many subscribers; bidding isn't a broadcast problem.
Multiple writers racing for one highest-bid slot is exactly what the contention pattern addresses.
CQRS scales read and write models separately, but it doesn't decide who wins the bid.
scenario: 在线拍卖同一场次里多人同时出价，所有人都在抢同一个「当前最高价」这一个位置。
scenario_en: In a single auction multiple people bid at the same instant, all fighting over the one slot that is the current highest bid.

q: 当前最高价 $10，A 出 $100、B 紧接着出 $20。没有并发控制时最坏会怎样？
q_en: If the current highest bid is $10, A bids $100, then B bids $20, what is the worst case without concurrency control?
options: B 的 20 美元出价会被正确拒绝，因为读到了最新的 100 美元，系统运行正常
A 的 100 美元出价会因为并发冲突而丢失，这不是真正发生的情况
两个事务互相等待对方释放锁，系统发生死锁，这不是这里的故障模式
B 读到陈旧的 10 美元，20 大于 10 通过校验——两人都被接受、都以为自己在赢
why: B 基于过时读数（$10）通过了校验，于是 $100 和 $20 都被接受，拍卖出现两个「最高出价者」。B 本应和更新后的 $100 比较而被拒绝。
why_en: User B validates a twenty-dollar bid against a stale ten-dollar read, so both bids get accepted and two users each think they're winning.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as User A
    participant B as User B
    participant DB as Database
    A->>DB: 读最高价 = $10
    A->>DB: 写入 $100（接受）
    B->>DB: 读最高价 = $10（陈旧！）
    B->>DB: 写入 $20（错误地接受）
options_en: B's twenty-dollar bid is correctly rejected because B reads the updated hundred-dollar price, so the system works fine.
A's hundred-dollar bid is lost due to a concurrency conflict, which isn't actually what happens here.
The two transactions wait on each other's locks and the system deadlocks, which isn't the failure mode here.
B reads a stale ten-dollar price, twenty beats ten so it passes validation — both bids get accepted and both users think they're winning.

termDefinitions.meaning: 读到的是数据被更新之前的旧值，而不是最新写入的值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A stale read returns an old value from before the latest write instead of the current one.

optionExplanations: 这个结果得靠并发控制或强制重读才会发生；题目明说没有保护。
A 的写入并没消失，真正的问题是 B 拿旧值做了校验。
死锁要靠两边互相等锁才成立，这里的毛病是读到了旧数据。
B 读到的还是 $10，20 大于 10 就通过了，于是两条出价都被错误接受。
optionExplanations_en: That outcome needs concurrency control or a forced re-read; the prompt says there's none.
A's write isn't lost — the real bug is that B validated against a value that was already old.
Deadlock needs both sides waiting on each other's lock; the bug here is a stale read, not a lock wait.
B is still looking at $10, twenty beats ten so it passes, and both bids get wrongly accepted.
scenario: 在线拍卖的出价校验是「先读当前最高价，再比较后插入」，两次出价可能只差几毫秒。
scenario_en: Bid validation reads the current highest bid, compares, then inserts — and two bids can land milliseconds apart.

q: 有人认为「竞价其实不需要强一致，最终一致就够」，这个论点的实质与局限是？
q_en: What is the real point and limitation of saying auction bidding can use eventual consistency?
options: 论点无效——两个 bid 都被接受，会让最终赢家的判定结果出错，需要额外修正逻辑
论点成立——最终赢家不变，事后通知 B 即可；但它绕开核心难点，面试官通常仍要求强一致
论点有效，而且所有系统设计面试官都会直接采纳这个最终一致方案，这个断言太绝对
论点只在两人出价金额恰好完全相同的情况下才成立，这不是本题的前提条件
why: 两个 bid 都接受不影响最终结果，事后修正客户端即可——论点成立，但它绕开了核心难点，面试官通常仍要求强一致方案。
why_en: The eventual-consistency argument is valid since the winner is unchanged, but it dodges the hard part, so interviewers still expect strong consistency.
options_en: Invalid — accepting both bids would corrupt who is judged the final winner, needing extra fix-up logic.
Valid — the final winner is unchanged, so you can just notify B afterward; but it dodges the core difficulty, and most interviewers still expect a strong-consistency solution.
Valid, and every system design interviewer accepts this eventual-consistency approach outright, which overstates it.
It only holds when both bids happen to be for the exact same amount, a premise this problem never sets.
optionExplanations: 最终赢家其实还是按最高金额算，两笔出价都留着不一定会错认赢家。
这个说法站得住，但它避开了写路径的硬骨头，面试通常还是要你啃下去。
把「面试官都会接受」说死了——大多数场景下还是要看到强一致方案。
金额是否相等是另一条业务规则，不是这个论点能不能成立的前提。
optionExplanations_en: The final winner is still decided by the highest amount; keeping both submitted bids doesn't necessarily misjudge it.
The point holds, but it sidesteps the hard write-path problem, and interviewers usually still want it solved.
Claiming every interviewer accepts this is overreach — most rounds still expect a strong-consistency answer.
Whether amounts happen to be equal is a separate business rule, not a condition for this argument.
scenario: 在线拍卖面试里你想省掉锁：两个 bid 都先收下，事后再把客户端显示修正回来。
scenario_en: In the auction interview you want to skip locking entirely — accept both bids, then correct what the client shows afterwards.

q: 第一种保证竞价一致性的思路——行级锁方案——的流程是？
q_en: What is the flow for the row-locking approach to keeping bids consistent?
options: 开事务后 SELECT ... FOR UPDATE 锁住 bid 行，查最大值、比较、插入
不开事务，直接锁住整张 bids 表再插入新出价，会连累一堆无关拍卖的写入请求
先用 Redis 拿一把分布式锁，再对数据库执行插入，这是另一套跨进程协调方案
完全不加锁，直接插入新出价，靠唯一索引兜底去重，挡不住旧值校验通过的写入
why: 思路是用事务 + SELECT ... FOR UPDATE 把该拍卖的现有 bid 行全锁住，串行化「查最大 → 比较 → 插入」。但它有严重缺陷，不适合生产。
why_en: The row-locking approach wraps a transaction that locks the auction's existing bid rows, checks the max, and inserts the new bid before committing.
options_en: Begin a transaction, SELECT ... FOR UPDATE to lock the auction's bid rows, read the max, compare, then insert.
Skip the transaction and just lock the entire bids table before inserting, blocking unrelated auctions too.
Grab a Redis distributed lock first, then run the database insert — a separate cross-process approach.
Insert the new bid with no locking at all, relying on a unique index to deduplicate, which won't stop stale-max validation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在事务里给查询到的行加锁，阻止其他事务修改这些已有行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE locks the rows a query returns within a transaction, blocking other transactions from modifying them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一组数据库操作要么全部成功、要么全部回滚的原子单元。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A transaction is a group of database operations that either all succeed or all roll back together.

optionExplanations: 开事务锁住本拍卖的出价行，把查最大、比较、插入串成一条不被打断的操作。
全表锁连累了所有拍卖，热门拍卖会把毫不相关的拍卖也一起堵住。
分布式锁是另一套跨进程方案，这题问的是数据库自己的行锁怎么做。
唯一索引只挡得住重复请求，挡不住两笔金额各自拿旧最大值通过校验。
optionExplanations_en: Open a transaction, lock this auction's bid rows, and chain read-max, compare, and insert into one uninterrupted step.
A whole-table lock drags in every auction — a hot one would block totally unrelated auctions too.
A distributed lock is a separate cross-process approach; this card is about the database's own row lock.
A unique index only stops duplicate requests, not two amounts each passing against a stale max.
scenario: 在线拍卖 bids 存在单个 Postgres 里，要让「查最大价 → 比较 → 插入」三步不被并发穿插。
scenario_en: Auction bids live in a single Postgres instance, and you need read-max, compare, insert to run without another bid slipping in between.

scenario: 在线拍卖用事务里 SELECT ... FOR UPDATE 锁住 bids 表中该拍卖的已有行，再算 MAX、比较、插入。两人同一毫秒出价。
scenario_en: The auction wraps a transaction that uses SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the auction’s existing bid rows, then reads MAX, compares, and inserts. Two users bid in the same millisecond.
q: 为什么 SELECT ... FOR UPDATE 挡不住两笔并发出价同时插入？
q_en: Why does SELECT ... FOR UPDATE fail to stop two concurrent bids from both being inserted?
options: 它只锁住 SELECT 命中的已有行，别的事务照样能往同一拍卖插入新行
它会把整张 bids 表锁死，第二个事务直接死锁退出，出价被误报成失败
它的锁在 SELECT 语句返回那一刻就释放，事务剩下的部分完全没有保护
它只在可重复读隔离级别下生效，默认隔离级别里等同于一条普通查询
options_en: It only locks the existing rows the SELECT matched; other transactions can still insert new rows for the same auction.
It locks the whole bids table, so the second transaction deadlocks out and the bid is wrongly reported as failed.
Its locks are released the moment the SELECT returns, leaving the rest of the transaction unprotected.
It only takes effect under repeatable read; at the default isolation level it behaves like a plain query.
optionExplanations: 行锁的作用域是已存在的行，尚未写入的新行不在封锁范围内。
死锁是另一种故障；这里两笔事务都会顺利提交，谁都没被拒。
锁一直持有到 COMMIT，问题不在释放时机而在覆盖范围。
隔离级别管读的可见性，加锁语义在任何级别下都照常生效。
optionExplanations_en: A row lock only covers rows that already exist; a row not yet written is outside its reach.
Deadlock is a different failure; here both transactions commit happily and neither is rejected.
The lock is held until COMMIT, so the problem is its coverage, not when it is released.
Isolation levels govern read visibility; the locking clause works at every level.
why: 锁只覆盖已有行：两笔事务读到同一个 max、各自通过校验、各自插入，同一场拍卖冒出两个赢家。要真串行化必须另加机制。
why_en: The lock only covers rows that already exist, so both transactions read the same max, both pass validation, and both insert — leaving the auction with two winners.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在事务里给查询命中的已有行加锁，阻止其他事务修改它们。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE locks the existing rows a query returns so other transactions cannot modify them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一组数据库操作要么全部提交、要么全部回滚的原子单元。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A transaction is a group of database operations that either all commit or all roll back.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库对并发事务互相可见程度的设置，如读已提交、可重复读、可串行化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An isolation level sets how much concurrent transactions can see of each other, such as read committed, repeatable read, or serializable.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两个事务互相等待对方持有的锁，谁都无法推进，数据库只能杀掉其中一个。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A deadlock is when two transactions each wait on a lock the other holds, so the database must abort one of them.

scenario: 已确认 FOR UPDATE 锁不住并发 INSERT。仍想留在单库悲观锁路线上，让同一拍卖的出价一个接一个落地。
scenario_en: You have confirmed FOR UPDATE cannot block concurrent inserts, but you still want to stay on a single-database pessimistic-locking path where bids on one auction land one at a time.
q: 要让同一拍卖的出价插入真正串行化，还得加什么机制？
q_en: What extra mechanism actually serializes bid inserts for the same auction?
options: 对 auction_id 取一个 advisory lock，或改锁一行必然存在的代理行
把隔离级别提到 SERIALIZABLE，让数据库自己把并发插入排成一列
给 (auction_id, amount) 建唯一索引，让第二笔出价撞索引冲突报错
把事务超时调长，让后到的事务一直等前一笔提交完再执行插入
options_en: Take an advisory lock keyed on auction_id, or lock a proxy row that is guaranteed to exist.
Raise the isolation level to SERIALIZABLE and let the database order the concurrent inserts itself.
Add a unique index on (auction_id, amount) so the second bid fails on a key conflict.
Increase the transaction timeout so a later transaction simply waits for the earlier one to commit.
optionExplanations: 锁必须落在一个「一定存在」的对象上，键或代理行都满足这点。
数据库自动串行更省心，但会把重试和吞吐损失摊到所有事务上。
唯一索引只挡同额重复，两笔不同金额照样各自通过旧值校验。
超时长短决定等多久，不决定谁在等——没有锁就没有排队。
optionExplanations_en: The lock must sit on something guaranteed to exist, which both a key and a proxy row satisfy.
Letting the database serialize is less work, but it spreads retries and throughput loss across every transaction.
A unique index only blocks identical amounts; two different amounts still pass against a stale max.
A timeout controls how long you wait, not who waits — with no lock there is no queue at all.
why: FOR UPDATE 锁不到还不存在的行，所以要锁一个必然存在的对象；代价是应用得自己记得取锁，漏一处就前功尽弃。
why_en: FOR UPDATE cannot lock a row that does not exist yet, so you lock something that always exists — at the cost of every code path remembering to take that lock.
tradeoff: 显式取锁的可控范围 vs SERIALIZABLE 的全局串行代价
whenOtherWins: 写入量不大、冲突又少的库，直接开 SERIALIZABLE 让数据库自动串行更省事，代价是事务被回滚重试。

termDefinitions.meaningEn: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE locks the existing rows a query returns so other transactions cannot modify them.

termDefinitions.meaning: Postgres 提供的按任意整数键取的应用级锁，不绑定任何具体数据行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An advisory lock is an application-level Postgres lock taken on an arbitrary key rather than on a data row.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最严格的隔离级别，效果等价于所有事务一个接一个执行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SERIALIZABLE is the strictest isolation level; the result must match some order of running transactions one at a time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库对并发事务互相可见程度的设置，如读已提交、可重复读、可串行化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An isolation level sets how much concurrent transactions can see of each other, such as read committed, repeatable read, or serializable.

scenario: 行锁方案每次出价都锁住该拍卖 bids 表里的全部已有行。热门拍卖一周累积上千条出价，收官前每秒上百笔新出价。
scenario_en: The locking approach locks every existing bid row for the auction on each new bid; a hot auction accumulates thousands of bids in a week and takes hundreds per second before closing.
q: 随着一场拍卖的出价数增长，这个锁方案会怎样退化？
q_en: How does this locking approach degrade as an auction accumulates more bids?
options: 要锁的行数随历史出价线性增长，锁持有变长，出价排队直到超时
锁的行数不变，只是索引膨胀让 MAX 查询变慢，属于纯读性能问题
行数越多锁越分散，撞在同一行的概率下降，整体吞吐反而提升
退化只出现在写库的磁盘 IO 上，跟锁多少行无关，换 SSD 就能缓解
options_en: The number of locked rows grows linearly with bid history, locks are held longer, and bids queue until they time out.
The locked row count stays flat; only index bloat slows the MAX query, so it is purely a read-performance issue.
More rows spread the locks out, collisions on any single row drop, and overall throughput actually improves.
The degradation is only in write-path disk IO and has nothing to do with lock scope, so faster SSDs fix it.
optionExplanations: 锁范围本身随数据量长大，这是方案结构性的问题，不是调参能救的。
索引确实会长，但真正卡住的是被锁住的行不让别人写。
锁的是同一拍卖的全部行，参与竞争的事务只会更多不会更少。
磁盘 IO 是次要项，出价请求是在等锁，不是在等落盘。
optionExplanations_en: The lock scope itself grows with the data, which is structural rather than something tuning can fix.
The index does grow, but what actually stalls bids is that locked rows block other writers.
Every row of the same auction is locked, so contending transactions only increase.
Disk IO is secondary here; bid requests are waiting on locks, not on flushes.
why: 行锁两条原则是锁尽可能少的行、锁尽可能短的时间，这里两条都违反；竞价场景里出价变慢或超时是不可接受的体验。
why_en: Row locking has two rules — lock as few rows as possible and hold them as briefly as possible — and this design breaks both, which bidders feel as slow or timed-out bids.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在事务里给查询命中的已有行加锁，阻止其他事务修改它们。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE locks the existing rows a query returns so other transactions cannot modify them.

termDefinitions.meaning: Solid State Drive（固态硬盘）：基于闪存的磁盘，随机读写远快于机械盘。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A solid state drive is flash-based storage with far faster random access than a spinning disk.

scenario: 为了不再锁一大片 bid 行，把每场拍卖的当前最高价缓存进 Redis，出价路径不再回表算 MAX。
scenario_en: To stop locking a large set of bid rows, the current max bid for each auction is cached in Redis and the bid path no longer recomputes MAX from the table.
q: 把 max bid 放进 Redis 后，一笔出价的数据流是哪三步？
q_en: With the max bid cached in Redis, what three steps does an incoming bid take?
options: 读 Redis 里的最高价 → 更高就更新 Redis → 按接受或拒绝把这笔出价写库
先把出价写库 → 再回表算一次 MAX → 用算出的结果覆盖 Redis 里的最高价
读 Redis 最高价 → 锁住该拍卖全部 bid 行 → 校验通过后插入并释放锁
只写 Redis 不落库 → 拍卖结束时把最终最高价一次性写进数据库归档
options_en: Read the max bid from Redis, update Redis if the new bid is higher, then write the bid to the database as accepted or rejected.
Write the bid to the database first, recompute MAX from the table, then overwrite the max bid in Redis.
Read the max bid from Redis, lock all of the auction’s bid rows, validate, insert, and release the locks.
Write only to Redis during the auction and persist the final max bid to the database once when it ends.
optionExplanations: 读缓存、改缓存、写库三步，最高价的判断完全不碰 bids 表。
先写库再回表算 MAX，等于把被优化掉的那次全表聚合又请了回来。
还锁全部 bid 行就白缓存了，锁范围一点没缩小。
这是后面「以 Redis 为真相源」的变体，中途崩溃会丢掉整段出价记录。
optionExplanations_en: Read cache, update cache, write database — deciding the max never touches the bids table.
Writing first and then recomputing MAX brings back the very aggregation the cache removed.
Still locking every bid row wastes the cache entirely, since lock scope never shrinks.
That is the later "Redis as source of truth" variant, and a mid-auction crash loses the bid history.
why: 判断最高价从数据库搬到内存后，锁竞争消失了；但这条流程有两个写入点，Redis 改了库没写成时两边就对不上。
why_en: Moving the max-bid decision from the database into memory removes lock contention, but the flow now has two write points that can disagree.

termDefinitions.meaning: 单线程的内存键值存储，常用来放热点数据和计数器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is a single-threaded in-memory key-value store often used for hot data and counters.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在事务里给查询命中的已有行加锁，阻止其他事务修改它们。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE locks the existing rows a query returns so other transactions cannot modify them.

scenario: 最高价已缓存进 Redis，出价路径不再回表算 MAX，数据库里那一大片行锁的竞争消失了。
scenario_en: The max bid now lives in Redis, the bid path no longer recomputes MAX from the table, and the wide row-lock contention in the database is gone.
q: 缓存方案消掉了库内的锁竞争，把问题换成了什么？
q_en: The cache removed in-database lock contention — what problem did it create instead?
options: 换成数据库与缓存之间的一致性问题：缓存报的最高价库里可能不存在
换成缓存容量问题：拍卖一多，Redis 内存装不下全部历史出价记录
换成纯延迟问题：多一跳网络往返，出价的响应时间必然明显变差
换成权限问题：Redis 没有行级权限，任何服务都能改掉最高价字段
options_en: It becomes a consistency problem between database and cache: the cache can report a max bid that no row backs.
It becomes a capacity problem: with enough auctions, Redis memory cannot hold the full bid history.
It becomes purely a latency problem: one more network hop necessarily makes bid responses much slower.
It becomes an access-control problem: Redis has no row-level permissions, so any service can rewrite the max.
optionExplanations: 真相散在两个系统里，任何一边写失败都留下一个说不清的状态。
缓存里每场拍卖只存一个数字，内存根本不是这里的瓶颈。
内存访问是毫秒级的，这一跳不是这个方案被放弃的原因。
权限是部署边界问题，跟这个方案换来的核心风险无关。
optionExplanations_en: Truth now lives in two systems, and a failed write on either side leaves a state nobody can reconcile.
The cache stores one number per auction, so memory is nowhere near the bottleneck.
An in-memory hop costs milliseconds and is not why this design gets abandoned.
Permissions are a deployment boundary concern, unrelated to the risk this design introduces.
why: 库内一致性问题被换成了库与缓存之间的一致性问题：Redis 更新成功而落库失败时，缓存显示的最高价对应不到任何一条 bid。
why_en: Consistency inside the database is traded for consistency between database and cache: if Redis updates but the database write fails, the displayed max bid matches no stored bid.

termDefinitions.meaning: 单线程的内存键值存储，常用来放热点数据和计数器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is a single-threaded in-memory key-value store often used for hot data and counters.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一旦系统回执成功，数据在崩溃后仍然存在，不会丢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Durability means that once the system acknowledges a write, the data survives a crash.

scenario: Redis 里存着每场拍卖的最高价，出价要做「读当前最高价 → 更高才写回」。两笔出价可能落在同一微秒。
scenario_en: Redis holds each auction’s max bid and a bid must read the current max and write back only if it is higher; two bids can land in the same microsecond.
q: 这段读改写为什么必须用 Lua 脚本而不是 MULTI/EXEC？
q_en: Why must this read-modify-write use a Lua script instead of MULTI/EXEC?
options: MULTI/EXEC 没法在同一事务里读出一个值、再按它的大小决定写不写
MULTI/EXEC 在集群模式下被整个禁用，只有脚本能跨槽位执行多条命令
Lua 脚本会绕开 Redis 的单线程模型，用多核并行把比较算得更快一些
MULTI/EXEC 缺少持久化保证，排队中的命令在实例崩溃时会整批丢失
options_en: MULTI/EXEC cannot read a value and then decide whether to write based on that value inside the same transaction.
MULTI/EXEC is disabled entirely in cluster mode, so only scripts can run multiple commands across slots.
A Lua script bypasses Redis’s single-threaded model and uses multiple cores to run the comparison faster.
MULTI/EXEC has no durability guarantee, so queued commands are lost as a batch when the instance crashes.
optionExplanations: 排队执行拿不到中间结果，条件判断就无从谈起。
槽位限制确实存在，但这里的障碍是条件写而不是键的分布。
脚本恰恰是靠单线程才原子，并没有引入任何并行。
持久化配置与两者的原子性无关，这是把话题岔到了落盘。
optionExplanations_en: Queued commands never expose an intermediate result, so a conditional write is impossible.
Slot limits are real, but the blocker here is the conditional write, not key distribution.
The script is atomic precisely because Redis is single-threaded; no parallelism is involved.
Persistence settings have nothing to do with atomicity here; this changes the subject to flushing.
why: Redis 单线程把整段 Lua 一次跑完，读改写因此成为一次不可打断的 compare-and-set；MULTI/EXEC 只能批量排队，看不到中间值。
why_en: Redis runs the whole Lua script in one uninterrupted single-threaded pass, which turns the read-modify-write into an atomic compare-and-set that MULTI/EXEC cannot express.
codeSample:
-- 原子地比较并设置最高价
local current_max_bid = tonumber(redis.call('GET', auction_key) or '0')
local proposed_bid_amount = tonumber(proposed_bid)

if proposed_bid_amount > current_max_bid then
    redis.call('SET', auction_key, proposed_bid_amount)
    return true   -- 出价被接受
else
    return false  -- 已被别人抬价，拒绝
end

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is a single-threaded in-memory key-value store often used for hot data and counters.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 用 EVAL 执行的一段脚本，整段在服务端一次跑完不被打断。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Lua script runs on the Redis server through EVAL and executes to completion without interruption.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 把多条命令排队后一次性执行的批处理事务，拿不到中间结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MULTI/EXEC queues several Redis commands and runs them in one batch, without exposing intermediate results.

termDefinitions.meaning: Compare-And-Set（比较并设置）：读到旧值后只在值没变时才写入新值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Compare-and-set reads a current value and writes the new one only if the value has not changed.

scenario: 最高价在 Redis、出价记录在关系库。三种折中都试过：异步落库、先改缓存写库失败再回滚、先写库再更新缓存失败就失效。
scenario_en: The max bid sits in Redis while bids live in a relational database, and all three compromises have been tried: async persistence, cache-first with rollback, and database-first with cache invalidation.
q: 为什么 Redis 加关系库这条路最终仍然不干净？
q_en: Why does the Redis-plus-relational-database path still not come out clean?
options: Redis 不支持两阶段提交，三种折中都留着一个「一边成了一边没成」的窗口
Redis 的 Lua 脚本其实不是原子的，读改写本身随时可能被别的命令穿插
关系库的事务不支持回滚，缓存改完之后库这边没有办法撤销已提交的写
Redis 的持久化是异步的，所以最高价一定要比数据库晚好几秒才会可见
options_en: Redis does not support two-phase commit, so all three compromises leave a window where one side succeeded and the other did not.
Redis Lua scripts are not actually atomic, so the read-modify-write can be interleaved by other commands.
Relational transactions cannot roll back, so once the cache changes the database write can never be undone.
Redis persistence is asynchronous, so the max bid is always visible several seconds later than in the database.
optionExplanations: 缺的是跨系统的提交协议，不是任何一边自己的原子性不够。
脚本内部是原子的；问题出在脚本之外的那次数据库写。
回滚恰恰是关系库最擅长的事，它管不了库外的 Redis。
可见性延迟是性能话题，这里争的是两边会不会永久不一致。
optionExplanations_en: What is missing is a cross-system commit protocol, not atomicity on either side alone.
The script itself is atomic; the exposure is the database write that happens outside it.
Rollback is exactly what a relational database does well — it just cannot reach into Redis.
Visibility lag is a performance topic; the argument here is about permanent divergence.
why: 需要跨系统原子性时，先问能不能重构成把状态收进单一系统；Redis 与关系库之间没有分布式事务，任何写入顺序都留窗口。
why_en: When you need atomicity across two systems, first ask whether the state can be restructured into one, because Redis and a relational database share no distributed transaction.
tradeoff: 跨系统原子性的复杂度 vs 把状态收进单一系统
whenOtherWins: 若能接受竞价期间以 Redis 为真相源、异步落库，性能优先的场景里这套折中仍然务实，代价是崩溃时可能丢最近的出价。

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is a single-threaded in-memory key-value store often used for hot data and counters.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Lua script runs on the Redis server through EVAL and executes to completion without interruption.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two-phase commit is a distributed transaction protocol where a coordinator asks every participant to prepare, then commits only if all agree.

scenario: 缓存路线因为跨系统一致性被放弃。目标是既不锁一大片行，也不再引入第二个存储系统。
scenario_en: The cache path was dropped over cross-system consistency; the goal is to avoid locking many rows without introducing a second storage system.
q: 最终方案把当前最高价放在哪，出价事务锁什么？
q_en: Where does the final design keep the current max bid, and what does the bid transaction lock?
options: 放在 Auction 表的 max_bid 列上，事务只锁这一行，写完 bid 更新它再提交
放在 bids 表的一条汇总行上，事务锁汇总行的同时也锁住该拍卖的历史出价
仍然放在 Redis，改成同步双写，事务提交前必须等 Redis 返回确认才 COMMIT
放在只读副本上预先算好，主库事务里直接读副本的结果，因此不需要加锁
options_en: On a max_bid column of the Auction table; the transaction locks that single row, writes the bid, updates it, and commits.
On a summary row in the bids table; the transaction locks that summary row and the auction’s historical bids together.
Still in Redis, but with synchronous dual writes so the transaction waits for a Redis ack before committing.
Precomputed on a read replica, so the primary’s transaction reads the replica result and needs no locking at all.
optionExplanations: 一行、几毫秒，锁的两条原则第一次同时满足。
还捎带锁历史行就退回了老问题，锁范围又跟出价数挂钩。
同步双写并不能让两个系统原子提交，失败窗口照样在。
副本天然滞后，拿它校验最高价会放过本该被拒的出价。
optionExplanations_en: One row, a few milliseconds — the first design that satisfies both locking rules at once.
Locking the history too walks back into the old problem, tying lock scope to bid count again.
Synchronous dual writes still cannot commit two systems atomically; the failure window remains.
A replica lags by nature, so validating against it lets through bids that should be rejected.
why: 把 Auction 表当缓存用：最高价和 bid 在同一个库里，一个事务就保证一致；代价是这一行成了该拍卖所有出价的串行点。
why_en: The Auction table acts as the cache: max bid and bids live in one database so a single transaction keeps them consistent, at the cost of making that row a serialization point.
tradeoff: 单行短事务的锁开销 vs 独立缓存带来的跨系统一致性
whenOtherWins: 当最高价的读 QPS 远高于写、单行变成读热点时，前面挡一层缓存仍然值得，代价是一致性要自己补。

termDefinitions.meaningEn: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE locks the existing rows a query returns so other transactions cannot modify them.

scenario: max_bid 已经放在 Auction 表上。想彻底不取悲观锁，改成读到 max_bid 之后带条件更新。
scenario_en: max_bid already lives on the Auction table, and you want to drop pessimistic locking entirely by reading max_bid and then doing a conditional update.
q: OCC 拿什么当版本号，条件更新失败了怎么办？
q_en: What does OCC use as the version here, and what happens when the conditional update fails?
options: 拿读到的 max_bid 当版本号，UPDATE 加同值条件，影响 0 行就整段重试
拿一个自增 version 列当版本号，UPDATE 时把它加一，更新失败就直接向用户报错
拿 bid_time 时间戳当版本号，条件是新出价的时间晚于表里记录的最后出价时间
拿行的隐藏事务号当版本号，冲突交给数据库自己检测并把冲突方阻塞到成功为止
options_en: Use the max_bid you read as the version, add it as a condition on the UPDATE, and retry the whole sequence when zero rows change.
It uses an auto-incrementing version column, bumps it on UPDATE, and returns an error to the user when the update fails.
It uses the bid_time timestamp as the version, requiring the new bid to be later than the last recorded bid time.
It uses the row’s hidden transaction id as the version and lets the database detect conflicts and block the loser until it succeeds.
optionExplanations: 值本身就是版本，省掉了额外的版本列。
独立 version 列也可行，但一冲突就报错会把正常的抬价误判成失败。
时钟不可靠，同一毫秒的两笔出价用时间戳分不出先后。
让数据库阻塞冲突方就回到了悲观锁，不再是乐观并发。
optionExplanations_en: The value itself is the version, which saves adding a separate version column.
A dedicated version column also works, but erroring on the first conflict turns a normal outbid into a failure.
Clocks are unreliable, and two bids in the same millisecond cannot be ordered by timestamp.
Letting the database block the loser is pessimistic locking again, not optimistic concurrency.
why: 当前 max_bid 就是版本：条件 UPDATE 影响 0 行说明期间有人抬了价，于是整段从读 auction 行重新走一遍再提交。
why_en: The current max_bid is the version: if the conditional UPDATE touches zero rows, someone outbid in between, so the whole sequence restarts from reading the auction row.
codeSample:
-- 只在 max_bid 没被别人改过时才更新
UPDATE auctions
SET max_bid = :new_bid
WHERE id = :auction_id
  AND max_bid = :original_max_bid;
-- 影响 0 行 = 期间有人抬价，从读 auction 行整段重试

termDefinitions.meaning: Optimistic Concurrency Control（乐观并发控制）：不加锁，提交时用版本条件检测冲突，冲突则重试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Optimistic concurrency control takes no locks and instead detects conflicts at write time with a version condition, retrying on failure.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: A transaction is a group of database operations that either all commit or all roll back.

scenario: 同一场拍卖上两笔出价撞在同一毫秒的情况相对罕见，绝大多数出价彼此并不冲突。
scenario_en: Two bids colliding within the same millisecond on one auction is relatively rare; the vast majority of bids do not conflict at all.
q: 在冲突罕见这个前提下，OCC 相比悲观行锁赢在哪、代价是什么？
q_en: Given that conflicts are rare, what does OCC win over pessimistic row locking, and at what cost?
options: 赢在常态路径完全不取锁，代价是偶发冲突时要整段重试
赢在冲突时不用重试，代价是每笔出价都要先取一次行锁
赢在写吞吐不再受磁盘限制，代价是最高价有可能读到旧值
赢在能跨多个分片保持原子，代价是要引入两阶段提交协议
options_en: It takes no lock on the common path, at the cost of retrying the whole sequence when a conflict does occur.
It avoids retries on conflict, at the cost of taking a row lock before every single bid.
Its write throughput is no longer disk-bound, at the cost of sometimes reading a stale max bid.
It keeps atomicity across shards, at the cost of introducing a two-phase commit protocol.
optionExplanations: 不冲突就一路直行，冲突了才付重试的钱。
这是悲观锁的形状：把成本前置到每一笔出价上。
磁盘不是这里的瓶颈，条件 UPDATE 读到的也不是旧值。
跨分片原子是另一个问题，OCC 解的是单行并发。
optionExplanations_en: No conflict means a straight path; you only pay for a retry when one actually happens.
That is the pessimistic shape: the cost is paid up front on every bid.
Disk is not the bottleneck here, and a conditional UPDATE does not act on a stale value.
Cross-shard atomicity is a different problem; OCC addresses single-row concurrency.
why: OCC 的适用前提就是冲突罕见：常态一把锁都不取；一旦同一拍卖长期高频撞价，重试的浪费会反过来超过取锁的开销。
why_en: OCC assumes conflicts are rare so the common path takes no lock; once one auction sees constant collisions, wasted retries cost more than simply taking the lock.
tradeoff: 无锁的常态吞吐 vs 冲突时的重试成本
whenOtherWins: 同一拍卖长期高频撞价时 OCC 重试率飙升，改用只锁 Auction 单行的悲观锁反而更稳定可预测。

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Optimistic concurrency control takes no locks and instead detects conflicts at write time with a version condition, retrying on failure.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two-phase commit is a distributed transaction protocol where a coordinator asks every participant to prepare, then commits only if all agree.

scenario: 出价由 Bid Service 同步写库。收官阶段某台 Bid Service 进程崩溃，手上正在处理的几笔出价还没落库。
scenario_en: Bids are written synchronously by the Bid Service; near closing time one Bid Service process crashes with several in-flight bids not yet persisted.
q: 为什么要在 Bid Service 之前先把出价写进持久消息队列？
q_en: Why should bids be written into a durable message queue before the Bid Service touches them?
options: 队列本身就是持久存储：服务整个崩掉，出价仍留在队列里等着重放
队列能把出价按金额排序，服务恢复以后可以直接拿到最高的那一笔
队列会自动去重，服务崩溃后的重放因此不会产生重复的出价记录
队列能代替服务把出价直接写进数据库，恢复期间落库完全不受影响
options_en: The queue is itself durable storage: even if the whole service dies, the bids stay in the queue waiting to be replayed.
The queue sorts bids by amount, so after recovery the service can pick up the highest one directly.
The queue deduplicates automatically, so replaying after a crash cannot create duplicate bid records.
The queue writes bids into the database on the service’s behalf, so persistence continues during recovery.
optionExplanations: 写进队列的那一刻出价就已经安全，之后崩谁都不丢。
队列按到达顺序保序，不按业务字段排序。
重放的幂等要业务自己保证，队列不替你做。
队列只负责存和投递，写库仍然是消费者的活。
optionExplanations_en: The bid is safe the moment it lands in the queue; nothing is lost by a later crash.
The queue preserves arrival order, not an ordering by business fields.
Idempotent replay is the application’s job; the queue does not do it for you.
The queue only stores and delivers; writing to the database is still the consumer’s work.
why: 丢一条出价等于告诉用户「你赢了但没赢」，durability 是硬需求；队列 ack 即落盘，消费者崩溃只是延后处理而不是丢数据。
why_en: Losing one bid means telling a user they lost an auction they won, so durability is a hard requirement; once the queue acks, a crash only delays processing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一旦系统回执成功，数据在崩溃后仍然存在，不会丢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Durability means that once the system acknowledges a write, the data survives a crash.

termDefinitions.meaning: 接收方告诉发送方「这条消息我已经收下并落盘」的回执。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ack is the receiver telling the sender that the message has been accepted and persisted.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把消息按分区落盘并复制的分布式日志型消息队列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed log-style message queue that persists messages to disk per partition and replicates them.

scenario: 一场热门拍卖进入最后几分钟，出价从每秒几十笔飙到每秒几千笔，远超 Bid Service 的处理能力。
scenario_en: A hot auction enters its final minutes and bids jump from dozens to thousands per second, far beyond what the Bid Service can process.
q: 没有消息队列时，面对这段尖峰只剩哪三个坏选择？
q_en: Without a message queue, which three unacceptable options are left for this surge?
options: 丢掉超出的出价、扛不住直接崩溃、或按峰值长期超额扩容
降低出价校验强度、缩短事务时间、或临时关掉实时价格广播
把出价改成批量提交、加大数据库连接池、或把读流量切到只读副本
对出价限流、给老用户优先通行、或把尖峰流量导到另一个地域机房
options_en: Drop the excess bids, crash under the load, or permanently over-provision for the peak.
Weaken bid validation, shorten transactions, or temporarily switch off real-time price broadcasting.
Batch the bid writes, enlarge the database connection pool, or move read traffic to a replica.
Rate-limit bids, prioritize long-time users, or route the surge to another region.
optionExplanations: 三个都踩红线：丢数据、宕机、或为几分钟高峰全年付钱。
这些是调优手段，几十倍的落差不是调参能吸收的。
批量和连接池能提一点上限，救不了一个数量级的尖峰。
限流本质就是丢出价，只是换了个说法；导流也搬不走峰值。
optionExplanations_en: All three cross a red line: lose data, go down, or pay year-round for a few minutes of peak.
These are tuning knobs, and a tens-of-times gap cannot be absorbed by tuning.
Batching and bigger pools raise the ceiling slightly but not by an order of magnitude.
Rate limiting is dropping bids under another name, and rerouting does not remove the peak.
why: 队列把尖峰摊平：出价先落盘排队，消费者按自己的节奏消化；代价是队列积压期间出价确认与实际入账之间会拉开延迟。
why_en: The queue flattens the surge by persisting bids first and letting consumers drain at their own pace, at the cost of a growing gap between acknowledgement and processing during backlog.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把消息按分区落盘并复制的分布式日志型消息队列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed log-style message queue that persists messages to disk per partition and replicates them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一旦系统回执成功，数据在崩溃后仍然存在，不会丢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Durability means that once the system acknowledges a write, the data survives a crash.

scenario: 两个用户对同一场拍卖出了完全一样的金额，规则是先到先赢。出价先进 Kafka，再由多个消费者实例并行处理。
scenario_en: Two users bid the exact same amount on one auction and the rule is first-come-first-served; bids go into Kafka first and are then processed by several consumer instances in parallel.
q: 分区键选什么才能让同一拍卖的出价按到达顺序处理？
q_en: Which partition key keeps one auction’s bids processed in arrival order?
options: 按 auctionId 分区，同一场拍卖的出价全落同一分区，分区内保序
按 userId 分区，同一用户的出价保序，不同用户之间再按时间戳排
只保留一个分区并让单个消费者串行处理全平台所有拍卖的出价
不设分区键，在消费者侧按 bid_time 排序后再处理，恢复全局顺序
options_en: Partition by auctionId so every bid for one auction lands on the same partition, which preserves order within it.
Partition by userId so one user’s bids stay ordered, then order across users by timestamp.
Keep a single partition and let one consumer process every auction’s bids serially.
Use no partition key and sort by bid_time on the consumer side to recover a global order.
optionExplanations: 顺序保证的粒度是分区，所以分区键必须等于要保序的业务实体。
同额竞争发生在不同用户之间，按用户分区正好把它们拆开了。
单分区确实全局有序，但也把并行度砍成一，扛不住峰值。
生产者时钟各不相同，按时间戳排会把真正的先后判反。
optionExplanations_en: Ordering is guaranteed per partition, so the key must match the entity you need ordered.
Tied bids happen between different users, and keying by user splits exactly those apart.
One partition is globally ordered but cuts parallelism to one and cannot absorb the peak.
Producer clocks differ, so sorting by timestamp can invert the true arrival order.
why: 同额先到先赢压在「Kafka 只保证分区内有序」这条保证上；计数单位 = 分区数，它同时是消费并行度上限，跨拍卖照样并行。
why_en: Kafka only guarantees ordering within a partition, so the first-bid-wins fairness rule rests on that guarantee while different auctions still consume in parallel.
tradeoff: 同一拍卖内的顺序保证 vs 更均匀的分区负载
whenOtherWins: 如果业务不看重同额先到先赢，随机分区能让负载更均匀，也不会被某场超热门拍卖压出热点分区。

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed log-style message queue that persists messages to disk per partition and replicates them.

termDefinitions.meaning: Kafka 主题内部的有序日志片段，同一分区内的消息保证按写入顺序消费。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A partition is an ordered log segment inside a Kafka topic, and messages within one partition are consumed in write order.

scenario: 出价峰值约每秒 1.5 万笔，必须做到同一拍卖内保序且消息绝不丢失。候选是 Kafka、RabbitMQ、SQS。
scenario_en: Peak bid volume is about fifteen thousand per second, ordering within an auction is required, and no message may be lost; the candidates are Kafka, RabbitMQ, and SQS.
q: 为什么这套出价管线最后选了 Kafka？
q_en: Why does this bid pipeline settle on Kafka?
options: 它同时给到高吞吐、落盘复制的持久性、和按 auctionId 分区保序
它提供跨主题的分布式事务，能把入队和写数据库这两步放进同一个原子提交里
它支持按消息优先级投递，可以让金额更高的出价被优先消费和处理掉
它自带延时投递能力，可以直接拿来实现拍卖的动态结束时间和倒计时
options_en: It delivers high throughput, durability through disk persistence and replication, and partitioning by auctionId all at once.
It offers distributed transactions across topics so the enqueue and the database write commit atomically in one step.
It supports priority delivery so higher bid amounts get consumed and processed ahead of lower ones.
It has built-in delayed delivery, which can directly implement dynamic auction end times and countdowns.
optionExplanations: 三条正好对上本题的三个硬需求：量、不丢、保序。
入队与落库跨了两个系统，仍然没有统一提交这回事。
优先级投递会破坏先到先赢，正好和公平性规则冲突。
延时是后面结束拍卖那题的需求，不是选队列的理由。
optionExplanations_en: Those three map exactly onto the three hard requirements: volume, no loss, and ordering.
Enqueue and database write span two systems, so there is still no single commit.
Priority delivery breaks first-come-first-served and conflicts with the fairness rule.
Delayed delivery belongs to the auction-ending problem, not to picking a queue.
why: 三个需求各对应一条能力：峰值靠吞吐、不丢靠落盘复制、公平靠分区保序；代价是要自己运维一个 Kafka 集群。
why_en: Each requirement maps to one capability — throughput for the peak, disk plus replication for durability, partitioning for fairness — at the cost of operating a Kafka cluster yourself.
tradeoff: Kafka 的分区保序与吞吐 vs 托管队列省掉的运维成本
whenOtherWins: 如果吞吐只有每秒几百笔、也不需要按键保序，SQS 这类托管队列免去集群运维更划算。

termDefinitions.meaning: 把消息按分区落盘并复制的分布式日志型消息队列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed log-style message queue that persists messages to disk per partition and replicates them.

termDefinitions.meaning: Kafka 主题内部的有序日志片段，同一分区内的消息保证按写入顺序消费。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A partition is an ordered log segment inside a Kafka topic, and messages within one partition are consumed in write order.

termDefinitions.meaning: Simple Queue Service：AWS 的托管消息队列服务，免集群运维。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Simple Queue Service is AWS’s managed message queue, so you do not run the cluster yourself.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于队列与交换机路由的传统消息中间件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RabbitMQ is a traditional message broker built around queues and exchange-based routing.

scenario: 出价链路改成：API 网关 → producer → Kafka → Bid Service 消费 → 写库。用户点完出价要立刻看到反馈。
scenario_en: The bid path is now API gateway to producer to Kafka to Bid Service to database, and the user expects immediate feedback after tapping bid.
q: 有了队列后系统在哪个时刻回执用户，失败靠什么兜底？
q_en: With the queue in place, when does the system respond to the user, and what covers a failure?
options: Kafka 确认写入成功就回执「已收到」，后续消费失败可以从队列重放
等 Bid Service 把出价写库成功后再回执，队列只用来平滑消费者负载
producer 把消息交给网卡后立刻回执，投递失败由客户端自己重试提交
等 SSE 把新的最高价推回客户端之后才回执，保证看到的就是最终结果
options_en: Once Kafka acks the write, the user is told the bid was received, and any later processing failure can be replayed from the queue.
The response waits until the Bid Service has written the bid to the database; the queue only smooths consumer load.
The producer responds as soon as the message is handed to the network card, and the client retries on delivery failure.
The response waits until SSE has pushed the new max bid back, so the user sees the final result.
optionExplanations: 落盘 ack 是持久性的分界线，过了这条线才敢回执。
等落库就把队列的削峰收益抵消了，尖峰时用户仍要排队等。
交给网卡不等于对方收到，崩在半路这笔出价就没了。
广播是异步补通知的手段，不是回执的前置条件。
optionExplanations_en: The disk ack is the durability boundary, and only past it is a response safe to send.
Waiting for the database write cancels the queue’s smoothing benefit and makes users wait at peak.
Handing bytes to the network card is not delivery; a crash in between loses the bid.
Broadcasting is how the result is delivered asynchronously, not a precondition for the receipt.
why: Kafka 落盘 ack 就可以回执，消费者按自身节奏处理、失败重放；代价是「已收到」不等于「已接受」，结果得靠后面的出价广播补回来。
why_en: The response goes out once Kafka has persisted the bid, and consumers process at their own pace with replay on failure — but received is not accepted, so the outcome must be broadcast later.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed log-style message queue that persists messages to disk per partition and replicates them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 接收方告诉发送方「这条消息我已经收下并落盘」的回执。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ack is the receiver telling the sender that the message has been accepted and persisted.

termDefinitions.meaning: Server-Sent Events：浏览器用 EventSource 建立的单向长连接，只由服务端往客户端推。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Server-Sent Events is a one-way long-lived connection opened by the browser with EventSource, where only the server pushes data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一旦系统回执成功，数据在崩溃后仍然存在，不会丢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Durability means that once the system acknowledges a write, the data survives a crash.

scenario: 拍卖页每隔几秒轮询一次 GET /auctions/:id 拿最高价。热门拍卖每秒都有新出价，冷门拍卖几小时没动静。
scenario_en: The auction page polls GET /auctions/:id every few seconds for the max bid; hot auctions get new bids every second while quiet ones go hours unchanged.
q: 定时轮询在这两类拍卖上分别暴露出什么问题？
q_en: What problem does fixed-interval polling expose on each of these two kinds of auctions?
options: 热门拍卖更新不够快，冷门拍卖绝大多数请求查回来价格根本没变
热门拍卖会触发接口限流，冷门拍卖的响应会被 CDN 缓存成过期数据
热门拍卖会读到脏数据，冷门拍卖的连接会被中间代理提前掐断掉
热门拍卖的出价排序会乱掉，冷门拍卖的请求会因超时被反复重发
options_en: Hot auctions do not update fast enough, while on quiet auctions nearly every request comes back with an unchanged price.
Hot auctions trip API rate limits, while quiet auctions get stale responses cached by the CDN.
Hot auctions read dirty data, while quiet auctions have their connections cut early by an intermediate proxy.
Hot auctions get their bid ordering scrambled, while quiet auctions retry endlessly after timeouts.
optionExplanations: 一个是延迟太大，一个是请求全是空跑，两个病同时存在。
限流和 CDN 是可配置项，不是轮询本身的结构性缺陷。
轮询读的是已提交数据，脏读不会因为轮询而出现。
排序由写入路径决定，跟客户端多久拉一次没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: One side suffers latency, the other burns requests for nothing — both problems exist at once.
Rate limits and CDN behaviour are configuration, not a structural flaw of polling.
Polling reads committed data, so dirty reads do not arise from polling itself.
Ordering is decided on the write path and is unrelated to how often clients pull.
why: 轮询间隔既是延迟上限也是浪费来源：对秒级抬价的热门拍卖太慢，而绝大多数请求打到库里只是确认「没变」。
why_en: The polling interval is both the latency ceiling and the source of waste: too slow for auctions that move every second, while most requests hit the database only to confirm nothing changed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务端把请求挂着不立刻回，等到有新数据或超时才响应。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: With long polling the server holds the request open and responds only when new data arrives or a timeout fires.

scenario: 为了减少空转请求，服务端不再对「拿最高价」的请求立即返回，而是先把请求挂着。
scenario_en: To cut wasted requests, the server no longer answers a max-bid request immediately but holds it open instead.
q: 长轮询的服务端具体怎么处理一个拿最高价的请求？
q_en: How exactly does a long-polling server handle a request for the max bid?
options: 把请求挂起放进该拍卖的待响应表，有新最高价或 30-60 秒超时才返回
立刻返回当前最高价，并在响应头里带上服务端建议的下一次轮询间隔
把请求转成一条订阅记录写进 Redis，由后台任务定时批量回写给客户端
保持连接但每秒回一个心跳帧，把当前最新价格夹在心跳里持续下推给客户端
options_en: It parks the request in a pending map for that auction and responds only when a higher bid arrives or a 30-60 second timeout fires.
It returns the current max bid immediately and puts a suggested next polling interval in the response header.
It converts the request into a subscription record in Redis and lets a background job write batches back to clients.
It keeps the connection and sends a heartbeat every second, carrying the latest price along with each heartbeat.
optionExplanations: 挂起的请求按拍卖分组，新出价一来就统一响应这一组。
立即返回就退回了普通轮询，空跑请求一个都没省下。
写进 Redis 再定时回写，延迟又被批处理周期重新拉长。
每秒心跳属于服务端持续推送，那是 SSE 的形状不是长轮询。
optionExplanations_en: Parked requests are grouped per auction, and a new bid answers the whole group at once.
Answering immediately is plain polling again and saves none of the empty requests.
Writing to Redis and flushing on a timer reintroduces latency through the batch interval.
A per-second heartbeat is continuous server push, which is the SSE shape rather than long polling.
why: 服务端为每场拍卖维护一张待响应请求表：新出价被接受时统一响应全部等待者，客户端拿到结果后立刻发起下一次长轮询。
why_en: The server keeps a map of pending requests per auction, answers all waiters when a bid is accepted, and each client immediately opens the next long poll.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: With long polling the server holds the request open and responds only when new data arrives or a timeout fires.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is a single-threaded in-memory key-value store often used for hot data and counters.

scenario: 一场拍卖有 5 万人在长轮询等最高价。一笔新出价被接受，服务端同时响应了这 5 万个挂起请求。
scenario_en: Fifty thousand clients are long-polling one auction; a new bid is accepted and the server answers all fifty thousand pending requests at once.
q: 这一瞬间之后会发生什么，超时时长该怎么权衡？
q_en: What happens in the instant after that, and how should the timeout be tuned?
options: 5 万个客户端同时重连形成惊群，超时越短请求越多、越长遗漏窗口越大
5 万个连接被逐一关闭，超时越短越省内存、越长越容易触发接口限流
客户端会各自退避重连自然错峰，超时长短只影响服务端的内存占用量
重连会被负载均衡自动摊平，超时长短只决定客户端设备的电量消耗量
options_en: All fifty thousand clients reconnect at once as a thundering herd; shorter timeouts mean more requests while longer ones widen the miss window.
The connections close one by one; shorter timeouts save memory while longer ones are more likely to trip rate limits.
Clients back off and naturally spread out, so the timeout only affects server memory usage.
The load balancer smooths the reconnects automatically, so the timeout only affects client battery drain.
optionExplanations: 响应是同一时刻发出的，重连也就在同一时刻到达。
内存和限流是次生影响，真正的冲击是瞬时请求量。
客户端拿到数据就立刻重连，默认没有任何退避。
负载均衡摊的是机器间分布，摊不掉同一瞬间的总量。
optionExplanations_en: The responses go out at the same instant, so the reconnects arrive at the same instant too.
Memory and rate limits are secondary; the real hit is the instantaneous request volume.
Clients reconnect the moment they get data, with no backoff by default.
A load balancer spreads load across machines but cannot reduce the total in one instant.
why: 同时响应就会同时重连，这就是 thundering herd；超时窗口还会漏更新——刚超时后到达的出价要等下一轮才看得到。
why_en: Answering everyone at once makes everyone reconnect at once, and the timeout window also drops updates: a bid arriving right after a timeout is only seen on the next round.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: With long polling the server holds the request open and responds only when new data arrives or a timeout fires.

termDefinitions.meaning: 大量客户端在同一时刻被唤醒并同时发起请求，把服务端瞬间压垮。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A thundering herd is many clients waking at the same instant and hitting the server all at once.

scenario: 长轮询上线后要加机器：同一场拍卖的观众被负载均衡分散到 3 台服务器，而一笔新出价只会到达其中一台。
scenario_en: Scaling long polling out, viewers of one auction are spread by the load balancer across three servers, but a new bid only reaches one of them.
q: 为什么加机器本身解决不了，还得再引入什么？
q_en: Why does adding servers not solve this on its own, and what else is needed?
options: 每台只知道自己手上的挂起请求，要靠 Redis 或队列把出价广播给其余机器
每台的连接数上限不同，要靠一致性哈希把同一拍卖的观众固定到同一台机器上
负载均衡不支持长连接，要换成七层网关才能把挂起的请求正确路由回去
每台缓存的最高价会漂移，要靠定时任务从库里刷新各台机器上的本地副本
options_en: Each server only knows its own pending requests, so Redis or a queue must broadcast the new bid to the others.
Servers have different connection limits, so consistent hashing must pin all viewers of one auction onto a single server.
The load balancer does not support long-lived connections, so a layer-7 gateway is needed to route parked requests.
Each server’s cached max bid drifts, so a scheduled job must refresh the local copies from the database.
optionExplanations: 挂起请求是进程内状态，跨机通知只能靠外部协调层。
把一场拍卖钉死在一台上，超热门拍卖立刻变成单机热点。
四层负载均衡本来就能转发长连接，路由不是障碍。
定时刷新把延迟又拉回秒级，等于退回轮询。
optionExplanations_en: Pending requests are in-process state, so cross-machine notification needs an external coordination layer.
Pinning one auction to one server turns a very popular auction into a single-machine hotspot.
Layer-4 load balancers forward long-lived connections fine, so routing is not the blocker.
Refreshing on a timer pushes latency back to seconds, which is polling again.
why: 挂起请求是每台服务器的本地状态：计数单位 = 本机连接数，新出价只到达一台；跨机通知要额外协调层，代价是多一个组件和故障点。
why_en: Pending requests are per-server local state and a new bid lands on only one server, so cross-server notification needs an extra coordination layer — one more component and one more failure point.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: With long polling the server holds the request open and responds only when new data arrives or a timeout fires.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is a single-threaded in-memory key-value store often used for hot data and counters.
