termDefinitions.meaningEn: In publish/subscribe, a publisher sends one message to a channel and every instance subscribed to it receives a copy.

scenario: 拍卖页只需要服务端把新的最高价推给浏览器，客户端不通过这条连接往回发任何数据（出价走普通 HTTP 接口）。
scenario_en: The auction page only needs the server to push new max bids to the browser; the client sends nothing back over that connection since bids go through a normal HTTP endpoint.
q: 推最高价这条通道该选 SSE 还是 WebSocket？
q_en: Should the max-bid push channel use SSE or WebSocket?
options: 选 SSE：通信本来就是单向的，它更轻量也更好实现
选 WebSocket：只有它能保持长连接，SSE 每次推送都要重新建立连接
选 WebSocket：双向通道能顺带让客户端从同一条连接把出价提交上来
选 SSE：因为它走 UDP，比 WebSocket 依赖的 TCP 推送延迟更低一些
options_en: Pick SSE: the communication is one-way anyway, and it is lighter and simpler to implement.
Pick WebSocket: only it holds a persistent connection, since SSE reconnects for every push.
Pick WebSocket: the bidirectional channel also lets the client submit bids over the same connection.
Pick SSE: it runs over UDP, so it pushes with lower latency than WebSocket’s TCP.
optionExplanations: 浏览器一个 EventSource 就能收流，服务端只管往里写。
SSE 同样是长连接，推一次并不需要重建。
出价走普通接口就够了，为一条上行通道换协议不划算。
SSE 建在 HTTP 之上，底层同样是 TCP，没有这条捷径。
optionExplanations_en: One EventSource in the browser receives the stream and the server just writes into it.
SSE is also a persistent connection; a push does not require rebuilding it.
Bids already go through a normal endpoint, so swapping protocols for one uplink is not worth it.
SSE runs on HTTP and therefore on TCP as well, so that shortcut does not exist.
why: 通信单向时 SSE 更合适：浏览器原生 EventSource 收流，不用自己管双向协议与心跳；代价是这条连接发不回数据。
why_en: When traffic is one-way, SSE fits better because the browser’s native EventSource receives the stream with no bidirectional protocol to maintain — at the cost of no client-to-server channel.
tradeoff: SSE 的单向轻量 vs WebSocket 的双向能力
whenOtherWins: 如果客户端也要通过同一条连接高频上行（比如聊天或实时协作），WebSocket 的双向通道才划算。

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Server-Sent Events is a one-way long-lived connection opened by the browser with EventSource, where only the server pushes data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端与服务端都能随时发消息的双向长连接协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a bidirectional long-lived connection where both client and server can send messages at any time.

termDefinitions.meaning: Transmission Control Protocol：面向连接、保证顺序与重传的传输层协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Transmission Control Protocol is a connection-oriented transport protocol that guarantees ordering and retransmits lost data.

termDefinitions.meaning: User Datagram Protocol：无连接、不保证送达与顺序的传输层协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The User Datagram Protocol is a connectionless transport protocol with no delivery or ordering guarantee.

scenario: 用户1 连在 Server A、用户2 连在 Server B，两人都在看拍卖 X。用户3 的出价被路由到 Server A 并被接受。
scenario_en: User 1 is connected to Server A and User 2 to Server B, both watching auction X, when User 3’s bid is routed to Server A and accepted.
q: 用户2 的页面此时会怎样，问题的根源在哪？
q_en: What does User 2 see at that moment, and where does the problem come from?
options: 用户2 一直停在旧价：Server B 不知道这笔出价，只会推自己手上的连接
用户2 会延迟几秒才看到：Server B 要等下一次数据库轮询才拿得到新价
用户2 会收到但金额是错的：两台服务器的最高价缓存互相覆盖掉了对方
用户2 的连接会被断开重连：负载均衡发现状态不一致就强制迁移这条连接
options_en: User 2 stays on the old price: Server B never learns about the bid and only pushes to its own connections.
User 2 sees it a few seconds late: Server B has to wait for its next database poll to pick up the new price.
User 2 gets a wrong amount: the two servers’ cached max bids overwrite each other.
User 2’s connection is dropped and reopened: the load balancer migrates it on detecting inconsistent state.
optionExplanations: 连接集合是进程内状态，Server B 手上根本没有这条消息。
如果还要轮询数据库，就已经不是推送方案了。
两台各自维护自己的连接，谈不上互相覆盖。
负载均衡看不到应用层状态，不会因此迁移连接。
optionExplanations_en: The connection set is in-process state, and Server B simply never receives the message.
If it still polls the database, this is no longer a push design at all.
Each server keeps its own connections, so there is nothing to overwrite.
A load balancer cannot see application state and will not migrate a connection over it.
why: SSE 的连接集合是每台服务器的本地状态，出价只到达 Server A；Server B 上的观众会一直停在旧价，直到自己刷新页面。
why_en: The SSE connection set is per-server local state and the bid only reaches Server A, so viewers on Server B sit on a stale price until they reload the page.

scenario: 1000 万个并发拍卖，每场生命周期内约 100 笔出价，平均一场跑一周。现在要从左到右逐个组件核对峰值需求。
scenario_en: There are ten million concurrent auctions, roughly one hundred bids over each auction’s life, and an average auction runs for a week; now every component is checked left to right against peak demand.
q: 峰值出价吞吐的估算式该怎么列？
q_en: How should the peak bid-throughput estimate be laid out?
options: 拍卖数×每场出价数÷周期得日均，再除一天秒数得均值，最后乘 10 倍峰值系数
拍卖数×每场出价数直接除以一天的秒数，得到的结果就是要设计的峰值吞吐
并发拍卖数就等于并发出价数，直接按 1000 万每秒去规划所有组件的容量
先按单台数据库的写入上限定容量，再反推整个系统总共能支撑多少并发拍卖
options_en: Auctions times bids per auction over the lifetime gives daily volume; divide by seconds in a day for the average, then multiply by a ten-times peak factor.
Auctions times bids per auction divided by seconds in a day gives the peak throughput to design for directly.
Concurrent auctions equal concurrent bids, so plan every component for ten million per second.
Fix capacity from one database’s write ceiling first, then work backwards to how many auctions the system supports.
optionExplanations: 先摊到一周得日均，再摊到秒，最后才补上峰值系数。
漏掉了一周的周期，日均会被高估七倍。
拍卖是并发的，出价不是；两者差着一周的时间跨度。
按现有硬件反推是本末倒置，需求应该先于选型。
optionExplanations_en: Spread over a week for the daily figure, then over seconds, and only then apply the peak factor.
Dropping the week-long lifetime overstates the daily volume sevenfold.
Auctions are concurrent, bids are not; the two differ by a week-long span.
Deriving demand from existing hardware inverts the order — requirements come before sizing.
why: 10M×100÷7 天 ≈ 1.4 亿 bids/天 ÷ 10 万秒 ≈ 1.4K bids/s，再乘 10 倍峰值系数 ≈ 15K bids/s；这个数是后面定分区数、实例数和分片的基数。
why_en: Ten million times one hundred over seven days is about 140 million bids a day, roughly 1.4 thousand per second, and a ten-times peak factor gives about 15 thousand bids per second to size everything else against.

termDefinitions.meaning: bids per second：每秒出价笔数，衡量写入吞吐的单位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Bids per second is the write throughput unit counting how many bids the system takes each second.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把消息按分区落盘并复制的分布式日志型消息队列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed log-style message queue that persists messages to disk per partition and replicates them.

termDefinitions.meaning: Kafka 主题内部的有序日志片段，同一分区内的消息保证按写入顺序消费。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A partition is an ordered log segment inside a Kafka topic, and messages within one partition are consumed in write order.

scenario: 每条 Auction 约 1KB，每条 Bid 约 500B，一场拍卖约 100 笔出价、跑一周，因此一年约 5.2 亿场拍卖。
scenario_en: An Auction record is about one kilobyte, a Bid about five hundred bytes, an auction takes about one hundred bids and runs a week, giving roughly 520 million auctions a year.
q: 一年的存储量怎么算，算完指向哪个真正的约束？
q_en: How is the yearly storage computed, and which real constraint does the result point to?
options: 按每场 1KB 加 100×500B 累加再乘年拍卖数，约 25TB/年，存储不是瓶颈
只按每场 1KB 乘年拍卖数，约 0.5TB/年，说明单机 SSD 完全够用不必分片
按峰值吞吐乘一年的秒数去估，约 500TB/年，必须先做冷热数据分层归档
存储量没法先验估算，应该先上线跑一个月再按实际增长曲线外推容量需求
options_en: Add one kilobyte plus one hundred times five hundred bytes per auction and multiply by yearly auctions: about 25 TB a year, so storage is not the bottleneck.
Multiply only one kilobyte by yearly auctions: about 0.5 TB a year, so one SSD suffices and no sharding is needed.
Multiply peak throughput by seconds in a year: about 500 TB a year, so cold-hot tiering must come first.
Storage cannot be estimated up front; run in production for a month and extrapolate from the real growth curve.
optionExplanations: 出价记录才是存储的大头，一场拍卖里它占 50KB。
漏掉了 100 倍的出价数据，结论也就跟着错了。
峰值只出现在收官那几分钟，拿它乘全年会高估一个量级。
容量估算就是要在选型前给出量级，等上线再说太晚。
optionExplanations_en: Bid records dominate storage: they account for fifty kilobytes of each auction.
Leaving out the hundredfold bid data makes the conclusion wrong too.
The peak only lasts the final minutes, so multiplying it across a year overstates by an order of magnitude.
Capacity estimation exists to give an order of magnitude before you pick components, not after launch.
why: 520M 场 ×(1KB + 0.5KB×100) ≈ 25TB/年，现代 SSD 撑得住；真正的约束是峰值 15K writes/s 的写吞吐，它才是逼出分片的那个数。
why_en: Five hundred twenty million auctions times one kilobyte plus fifty kilobytes of bids is about 25 terabytes a year, which modern SSDs handle — the real constraint is the fifteen thousand writes per second at peak.

termDefinitions.meaning: Terabyte（太字节）：1TB = 1024GB，衡量存储容量的单位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A terabyte equals 1024 gigabytes and is the unit used here for storage capacity.

termDefinitions.meaning: Solid State Drive（固态硬盘）：基于闪存的磁盘，随机读写远快于机械盘。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A solid state drive is flash-based storage with far faster random access than a spinning disk.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按某个键把数据水平切到多个数据库实例上，分摊读写压力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sharding splits data horizontally across database instances by a key so read and write load is spread out.

scenario: 峰值约每秒 1.5 万次写入，超出单台 Postgres 的承受范围；而一场拍卖的读写总是围绕同一个 auction_id。
scenario_en: Peak write load is about fifteen thousand per second, beyond one Postgres instance, while all reads and writes for an auction revolve around the same auction_id.
q: 分片键该选什么，为什么不用担心 scatter-gather？
q_en: Which shard key should be used here, and why is scatter-gather not a concern?
options: 按 auction_id 分片：一场拍卖的读写全落同一分片，不需要跨分片聚合
按 user_id 分片：出价方分布更均匀，代价是查一场拍卖要扇出到所有分片
按 bid_time 范围分片：新出价集中在最后一片，收官时热点全压在同一台
按 seller_id 分片：卖家维度的查询会更快，但大卖家会把单个分片压成热点
options_en: Shard by auction_id: all reads and writes for one auction land on the same shard, so no cross-shard aggregation is needed.
Shard by user_id: bidders spread evenly, at the cost of fanning out to every shard to read one auction.
Shard by bid_time range: new bids concentrate on the last shard, so closing traffic all hits one machine.
Shard by seller_id: seller-side queries get faster, but a large seller turns one shard into a hotspot.
optionExplanations: 分片键跟访问单元对齐，扇出就自然消失了。
拍卖页是最热的读，扇出到全部分片会被最慢的那片拖住。
时间范围分片让写入永远压在最新那一片上，分不掉压力。
卖家规模差异极大，按它切分的数据分布天生不均。
optionExplanations_en: Aligning the shard key with the access unit makes fan-out disappear on its own.
The auction page is the hottest read, and fanning out ties its latency to the slowest shard.
Range sharding on time pins all writes to the newest shard and spreads nothing.
Seller sizes vary enormously, so that key produces inherently skewed distribution.
why: 逼出分片的是写吞吐而不是存储；auction_id 让「读最高价 + 插出价 + 更新 max_bid」都留在一个分片内，OCC 的条件更新仍是单库事务。
why_en: Write throughput rather than storage forces sharding, and keying on auction_id keeps read-max, insert-bid, and update-max inside one shard so the OCC conditional update stays a single-database transaction.
tradeoff: 单场拍卖的数据本地性 vs 按用户维度查询要扇出
whenOtherWins: 如果主要查询是「某个用户的全部出价」，按 user_id 分片才不用扇出，代价是拍卖页要跨分片聚合。

termDefinitions.meaning: 按某个键把数据水平切到多个数据库实例上，分摊读写压力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sharding splits data horizontally across database instances by a key so read and write load is spread out.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次查询要扇出到所有分片再把结果汇总回来的模式，延迟由最慢分片决定。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Scatter-gather is fanning one query out to every shard and merging the results, so latency follows the slowest shard.

termDefinitions.meaning: Optimistic Concurrency Control（乐观并发控制）：不加锁，提交时用版本条件检测冲突，冲突则重试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Optimistic concurrency control takes no locks and instead detects conflicts at write time with a version condition, retrying on failure.

scenario: 1000 万场拍卖、上亿条 SSE 连接分布在几百台 Bid Service 上，而一笔新出价只会到达其中一台。
scenario_en: Ten million auctions and a hundred million SSE connections are spread over hundreds of Bid Service instances, yet a new bid only reaches one of them.
q: 怎么让所有持有相关连接的服务器都推到这笔新价？
q_en: How does every server holding a relevant connection get to push the new price?
options: 收到出价的机器发布到 Pub/Sub 频道，所有实例订阅后匹配本地连接再推
把全部 SSE 连接集中到一台专用广播服务器上，出价统一交给它负责推送
让每个客户端同时连上所有服务器，哪台收到出价就由哪台直接推给客户端
把最高价写进共享数据库，各台服务器定时轮询数据库变化后推给本地连接
options_en: The server that received the bid publishes to a pub/sub channel; every instance subscribes and pushes to its own matching connections.
Concentrate all SSE connections on one dedicated broadcast server and let it handle every push.
Have each client connect to every server, so whichever one receives the bid pushes directly.
Write the max bid to a shared database and have each server poll it and push to its local connections.
optionExplanations: 发布一次、所有实例收到，各自只处理手上那批连接。
一亿条连接放不进一台机器，这是被规模直接否掉的方案。
客户端连接数会乘上服务器台数，连接总量爆炸。
轮询数据库把延迟又拉回秒级，实时性需求没满足。
optionExplanations_en: Publish once, every instance receives it, and each only handles the connections it holds.
A hundred million connections do not fit on one machine, so scale rules this out immediately.
Client connections multiply by server count and the total connection load explodes.
Polling the database pushes latency back to seconds and misses the real-time requirement.
why: 一亿连接 ÷ 单机可承载连接数 = 需要的机器台数，一台装不下，所以必须跨机广播：发布一次、全体订阅者收到、各自匹配本地连接。
why_en: A hundred million connections cannot fit on one machine, so broadcasting must cross servers: publish once, every subscriber receives it, and each matches its local auction connections — at the cost of one more hop and one more component.
tradeoff: Pub/Sub 的扇出延迟 vs 集中广播的单点瓶颈
whenOtherWins: 如果连接数少到一台机器就装得下，直接在进程内维护连接集合，省掉 Pub/Sub 这一跳和它的运维。

termDefinitions.meaning: 发布者往频道发一条消息，所有订阅该频道的实例都会收到。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: In publish/subscribe, a publisher sends one message to a channel and every instance subscribed to it receives a copy.

termDefinitions.meaning: Server-Sent Events：浏览器用 EventSource 建立的单向长连接，只由服务端往客户端推。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Server-Sent Events is a one-way long-lived connection opened by the browser with EventSource, where only the server pushes data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把消息按分区落盘并复制的分布式日志型消息队列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed log-style message queue that persists messages to disk per partition and replicates them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 单线程的内存键值存储，常用来放热点数据和计数器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is a single-threaded in-memory key-value store often used for hot data and counters.

scenario: 规则改成「距最后一笔出价满一小时就结束」。要求结束时刻尽量准，且不能被一笔迟到的有效出价搞乱。
scenario_en: The rule becomes "end one hour after the last bid", the end time should be as precise as possible, and a late valid bid must not break it.
q: 要让结束时刻精确，延时任务方案的关键一步是什么？
q_en: For a precise end time, what is the key step in the delayed-task approach?
options: 出价时排一个一小时后触发的任务，触发时校验这笔 bid 是否仍是最新的
出价时把 end_time 往后推一小时，让 cron 每分钟扫一遍已过期的拍卖
出价时先取消上一个任务再排新任务，靠任务数恒为一来保证不会误触发
让客户端在页面上做倒计时，倒计时归零时由前端调用结束拍卖的那个接口
options_en: On each bid, schedule a task to fire an hour later, and when it fires check whether that bid is still the latest.
On each bid, push end_time an hour out and let a cron job scan every minute for expired auctions.
On each bid, cancel the previous task before scheduling a new one so exactly one task ever exists.
Let the client count down on the page and call the end-auction endpoint when it reaches zero.
optionExplanations: 校验最新性让多余的任务自己失效，不需要去取消它们。
这是够用的简单解，但结束时刻的精度被扫描间隔限住。
取消是分布式环境里最容易失败的一步，多一个不可靠依赖。
客户端时钟不可信，也可能页面早就关了，没人触发结束。
optionExplanations_en: Checking for the latest bid makes stale tasks no-ops, so nothing needs cancelling.
That is the good-enough simple solution, but the scan interval caps how precise the end time can be.
Cancellation is the step most likely to fail in a distributed setting and adds an unreliable dependency.
Client clocks are untrustworthy and the page may be closed, leaving nobody to trigger the end.
why: 延时调度器（Redis sorted set、库支持的作业队列或 Step Functions 的 Wait）到点触发，触发时若已有更新的出价就不结束；代价是多一个调度组件。
why_en: A delayed scheduler such as a Redis sorted set, a database-backed job queue, or a Step Functions wait state fires on time and simply does nothing if a newer bid exists, at the cost of one more component.
tradeoff: cron 扫描的简单 vs 延时任务的精确
whenOtherWins: 如果结束时刻差几分钟无所谓，每次出价更新 end_time 加定期 cron 扫描更简单，也不用维护调度组件。

termDefinitions.meaning: 按固定时间表周期性运行的后台任务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cron job is a background task that runs on a fixed repeating schedule.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 里按分值排序的集合，用时间戳当分值就能实现延时队列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Redis sorted set orders members by a score, so using timestamps as scores gives you a delayed queue.

termDefinitions.meaning: 单线程的内存键值存储，常用来放热点数据和计数器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is a single-threaded in-memory key-value store often used for hot data and counters.
